rule_evidence.definition:
When a character's eyes light up in excitement, with yellow four-pointed sparkles in the center of their eyes replacing their pupils. Sparkles may also appear around their head.
Do not confuse with sparkling eyes, which is for sparkles near the pupil rather than replacing it, or with star-shaped pupils or cross-shaped pupils, which is for characters with naturally star- or cross-shaped eyes, such as Nia Teppelin or Chinchou.

rule_evidence.definition:
A symbol drawn next to a character's head to represent laughter, mirth, happiness or chatting noise. Looks a bit like ╀─╀, but with a curved line. Commonly used for laughter or the noise of a crowd that happens in the background, or in a scene that is otherwise silent.
Not to be confused with the Chinese radical "艹 which is often used as a shorter and more euphemistic form of "cao (Chinese for "fuck") when typing/writing.

general:4-finger heart hands.name: 4-finger_heart_hands

rule_evidence.definition:
Heart hands made with only four fingers.
The heart is usually made with the thumb and index fingers or the index and middle fingers.
The remaining six fingers are most often fully stretched or clenched, but there are also cases where they are slightly bent. In this case, we need to consider whether the fingers are naturally bent due to our anatomy, or whether the rest of the fingers are also bent in a heart shape and are in the process of forming the original heart hand.

This feature is sometimes enhanced through makeup or cosmetic procedures to create a more pronounced look. Certain fashion styles, such as gyaru and jirai kei, may use eyeshadow under the eyes to accentuate this area.
In contrast, most Western cultures view puffy eyes as unattractive and as making a person look tired, older, or like they're having an allergic reaction.

Ahegao (アヘ顔, lit. "ahe face", where "ahe" is a sound effect for wild moaning) is an orgasmic facial expression where the eyes are rolled up, the mouth is open, and the tongue is sticking out. Frequently accompanied by blushing, drooling, sweating, raising the eyebrows, or a double V gesture.
This expression usually (but not always) indicates a state of exaggerated sexual pleasure. It can also indicate craziness, drug influence, or asphyxiation.
Not to be confused with torogao, which is an expression that usually indicates a state of trance-like pleasure. Ahegao is a more manic expression.

general:ahoge.name: ahoge

general:ahoge.meaning_en:
Literally "stupid hair", an ahoge is a single long lock of hair that sticks out of a character's head.
Use cowlick instead if it's short or thick tuft of hair rather than a long strand. Use antenna hair instead if there's two or more thin locks of hair instead of only one.
If the ahoge reflects the character's emotions, it may also be expressive hair.

general:ai ai gasa.name: ai_ai_gasa

rule_evidence.definition:
A drawing consisting of two lovers' names beneath a sketch of an umbrella. It is the Japanese equivalent of writing the lovers' names inside a heart as done in the West.
For two people sharing an actual umbrella, use the tag shared umbrella.
By the way, it's not written "愛愛傘" with "ai", the kanji for "love", but is variously written "相合傘", "相合い傘", "相々傘", and "相相傘". So the translation isn't really "love love umbrella" but more like "togetherness umbrella".

general:akanbe.name: akanbe

rule_evidence.definition:
A Japanese facial gesture that consists of pulling an eyelid down while sticking the tongue out. It is sometimes accompanied by the sound べえだ (beeda, pronounced "behhh-dah").
This gesture is also done in France and Québec, where it is accompanied by saying "mon oeil" ("my eye").
The gesture is a juvenile taunt or way of teasing someone - the Japanese equivalent of thumbing your nose at someone, or yelling "Nyah nyah nyah" or "Neener neener" or the like.

general:alcohol.name: alcohol
general:alcohol.explanation_zh: 酒瓶与酒杯的示意组合。

rule_evidence.definition:
Any drink that contains ethanol, a psychoactive drug that has a depressant effect. Drinking too much of it can cause drunkenness. Possible health effects can include the increased risk for cancer, alcoholism, liver cirrhosis, depression, ataxia, and many more.
In Japanese, the word sake (酒) refers to any alcoholic drink. In English and on Danbooru, sake specifically refers to Japanese rice wine. Therefore, care should be taken when tagging based on translated tags or commentary.

general:alley.name: alley
general:alley.meaning_en:
A narrow lane found in cities, often for pedestrians only, which usually runs between or behind buildings.
In older cities and towns in Europe, alleys are often what is left of a medieval street network, or a right of way or ancient footpath in an urban setting. In older urban development, alleys were built to allow for deliveries such as coal to the rear of houses. Alleys may be paved, or simply dirt tracks. A blind alley has no outlet at one end and is thus a cul-de-sac.

general:animal ears.meaning_en:

general:anime coloring.name: anime_coloring
general:anime coloring.meaning_en:
A style of coloring used in 2D anime, consisting of hard-edged highlights and shadows, as opposed to the soft, smooth shadows used in fully rendered art. Also known as cel-shading, it is the art style seen in most anime screenshots.
It is a step beyond flat color: instead of base colors without any shadows, there are highlights and shadows on top, but the shadows are still solid blocks of color rather than smooth gradients.
For the similar technique employed in 3D artwork, see cel rendering.

general:anna miller.name: anna_miller

rule_evidence.definition:
A chain of restaurants in Hawaii and Japan. The first branch opened in 1973 in Hawaii, then expanded to 25 locations in Japan later that year.
The chain is famous for its waitress uniforms, which consist of a high-waisted pink or orange dress framing the underbust, an attached apron, a white blouse, and a heart-shaped name tag.
Anna Miller's physical restaurants in Japan were once all closed by August 31, 2022, after which the Japanese franchise existed as an online shop until a new physical store in Tokyo was opened on February 13, 2026.

general:anti-aircraft gun.name: anti-aircraft_gun

rule_evidence.definition:
A stationary, emplaced weapon system designed to shoot down aircraft. It may consist of an artillery piece like the 8.8 cm Flak, or mounted machine guns like the ZPU series.
Somewhat different from similar-looking anti-tank gun because they are often depicted pointing upwards, showing their capability of high degree elevation.
For the mobile, land vehicular counterpart which has its gun design integrated instead of being mounted on a regular vehicle, use self-propelled artillery or self-propelled anti-aircraft weapon instead.

general:antlers.name: antlers

rule_evidence.definition:
A pair of branched solid bone horn-like structures that arise from the frontal bone on the head of animals of the deer family. Unlike horns, antlers are branched, quickly develop underneath a covering of furry skin called velvet, consist of dead bone once fully developed, and regularly shed over the course of the animal's life (most commonly every year).
Not to be confused with Eastern dragon horns, which also branch, but are thicker and are categorized as horns.

For the architectural feature by the same name, see arcade (architecture). For the large stationary video game machine that is often seen inside an arcade, use arcade cabinet.

general:arched crown.name: arched_crown

rule_evidence.definition: A crown consisting of multiple metallic arches converging where the orb of the crown, or monde, would be at the very top. The arches may or may not be lined with gems. The crown's cross, located atop the monde, would either be an actual cross to represent the Christian influence of monarchies, or can possess a different shape. The crown's cap is lined with velvet that has a ermine base, although there are arched crowns with no cap present. Red velvet is typical of real-like royal crowns, and are frequently the basic depiction for arched crowns in artwork.

general:aria company uniform.name: aria_company_uniform

rule_evidence.definition:
The uniform worn by the ARIA Company of Undine (aria) gondoliers  in ARIA (manga). It has 2 different variations depending on the season:
The summer version consists of a cropped white short-sleeved sailor shirt with a white sailor collar a patch with the company's emblem on the left sleeve and blue chevron (symbol)s on the other, worn over a long, white sleeveless dress.
The winter version replaces the sailor blouse with a white capelet with yellow/gold trim and a long-sleeved, high-collared white dress, a long-sleeved white undershirt and dark purple pantyhose.

general:baozi.name: baozi

rule_evidence.definition:
A type of steamed, filled bun or bread-like dumpling originating in China, with regional varieties in many world cuisines. There are many variations in fillings (meat or vegetarian) and preparation (usually steamed).
In China, it is known as baozi. It is derived from the traditional Chinese mantou, a steamed bun without fillings (although regionally mantou may refer to baozi as well).
In Japan, it is known as manjuu, the Japanese rendering of mantou. A meat-filled manjuu is a nikuman; those referred to as manjuu typically have a sweet filling.

general:bass guitar.name: bass_guitar

rule_evidence.definition:
A plucked string instrument, closely related to the guitar. See double bass for the traditional bowed string instrument.
A bass guitar can be distinguished from a standard guitar by the fact that it almost always has four strings, and four tuning pegs at the top of the neck, usually along one side or with two on each side directly opposed. The bridge is also much closer to the bottom of the body to accommodate the longer strings.
Acoustic basses feature a larger resonator body to better amplify lower frequencies and a longer neck compared to their acoustic guitar counterparts.

general:battle rifle.name: battle_rifle

Though battle rifles were highly supplanted in mainstream service by lighter assault rifles, many are still used in specialist roles (e.g. designated marksman) by many armed forces and police units.

general:bindi.name: bindi

rule.phrase: a colored bindi on the forehead

rule_evidence.definition:
A forehead mark that consists of a colored dot (or sticker) worn on the center of the forehead. It is worn by Hindus, Jains and Buddhists from the Indian subcontinent. The mark is always applied close to the eyebrows or in the middle of the forehead.
Note that China historically had a mark similar to the bindi, called the cinnabar mole (朱砂痣, zhushazhi) or the dot cinnabar (点丹 diandan). The cinnabar it was made from gave it the red pigment, but was highly toxic. It was used as a status symbol, with links to taoism.
Use forehead mark or circle facial mark instead if the image has no correlation

rule_evidence.passage:
[b]Bishounen[/b] (lit. "beautiful youth") is a Japanese term for a young man with an [[androgynous]], feminine-leaning beauty. The equivalent English concept is [b]pretty boy[/b].
Bishounen are usually drawn delicately, with a slender body, long silky or flowing hair, expressive eyes with long eyelashes, and no facial hair. They are often depicted as elegant, sensitive, refined, intelligent, or possessing a mysterious and brooding past.
In English-speaking circles, bishounen is used somewhat more loosely than it is in Japan, effectively used for any male character with a pseudo androgynous beauty, regardless of whether they are "shounen" (teenage boys) or not (so older variants, such as biseinen, bichuunen, and bidanshi, may be included).

Skin colored pure black, like coal or ebony. The opposite of white skin.
For the usual brown, use dark skin, very dark skin and/or tan as appropriate.

general:blood bag.name: blood_bag

rule_evidence.definition:
A small bag full of blood, which has been collected from the patient or from a blood donor in order to replace that patient's blood should there be a lot of blood loss during surgery, or from exsanguination due to a critical injury.
Different patients/donors' blood is collected, analyzed and grouped according to blood type, of which there are four: A, B, AB, and O depending upon inherited antigens. There is also the + and - status to indicate if the Rh factor (or Rhesus factor) is present.
Blood bags are often seen hanging from intravenous stands in hospitals near the patient's bed.

There is also the + and - status to indicate if the "Rh factor":http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rh_blood_group_system (or Rhesus factor) is present.
Blood bags are often seen hanging from [[iv stand|intravenous stands]] in hospitals near the patient's bed.

general:blunt bangs.name: blunt_bangs
general:blunt bangs.meaning_en:
A hairstyle where the bangs are cut in a sharp, straight line across the entire length of the forehead. Mutually exclusive with swept bangs and asymmetrical bangs.
Known in Japan as パッツン (pattsun).
When combined with long hair and blunt sidelocks, it becomes a type of hime cut. If the bangs are shaved or combed back at the temples, with the rest hanging loose at the forehead it may result in center-flap bangs.

Blush stickers may appear with or without any actual reddening of the character's skin.

general:body armor.name: body_armor

rule_evidence.definition:

If the armor looks archaic or medieval, use armor instead.

general:bokeh.name: bokeh

rule_evidence.definition:
A photographic effect where circular out-of-focus points of light appear in the background of the image.
Bokeh can represent known light sources in the background of an image, but can also occur in seemingly random places all over the image. The latter, known as orbs are from light reflected off of particles in the air which would otherwise not be visible.
Lens flare artifacts can look similar to bokeh, but are due to bright light being reflected inside the camera, and don't line up with the original light source (which may not even be visible in the image).

general:bokken.name: bokken

rule_evidence.definition:
A lethal kendo practice sword made of solid, heavy wood. It's shaped and balanced like a katana.
Bokken are normally used for solo training, not for sparring. For that, the shinai is used, as sparring with a bokken will usually lead to broken bones... or worse.
Legendary samurai swordmaster Miyamoto Musashi (real life) is said to have fought (and killed!) katana-wielding rival samurai by using just a bokken against them.

A knot generally featuring two loops and two loose ends. Bows will be seen on clothing (many serafuku have them), in hair, on panties and other lingerie, on shoes (shoelaces are usually tied in a bow), and pretty much any place that there is something that might be tied.

general:bride.name: bride

rule.phrase: the role or appearance of a bride

rule_evidence.definition:
A woman getting married in a wedding ceremony.
Bridalwear differs across cultures. Usually a bride in a western wedding wears a long white wedding dress, a bridal veil, and carries a bouquet of flowers. A Japanese bride wears a shiromuku (a white kimono with red trim), a wataboushi (a white hood), and may carry accessories tucked into their kimono, such as a folding fan, a hakoseko (a wallet), and a futokorogatana ("chest sword", a small dagger held in a purse).

general:bubble tea.name: bubble_tea

rule_evidence.definition:
Bubble tea (also known as "pearl milk tea", "tapioca tea", "boba tea", or simply "boba") is a type of tea-based drink invented in Taiwan. It consists of a mixture of tea, milk, or other flavorings, plus small black tapioca balls ("boba") that float at the bottom of the drink. The drink usually comes with an extra-large straw, used to suck up and chew the tapioca balls.
In 2019, bubble tea experienced a sudden boom in popularity in Japan, with a corresponding rise in fanart featuring the drink.

For the Jewish counterpart with seven or nine branches, see menorah.

general:candle.name: candle
general:candle.meaning_en:
An object made of wax with a string running from top to bottom which is set alight. Its most common shape is cylindrical.
Has seen more use in the past, but it is still used as a light source in some places, in religious ceremonies and as a symbol of different things such as hope.
If the candles are worn strapped to the head with a headband, there might be a reference to the youkai Hashihime, or the curse ritual Ushi no Koku Mairi (which also involves a mallet or hammer, a straw doll and nail (hardware)s).

general:candlelight.name: candlelight

rule_evidence.definition:

This tag is not to be used when there's merely a lit candle in the image. It needs to be a dark setting illuminated by the light given off by at least one candle.

general:candlestand.name: candlestand

rule_evidence.definition:
A device that holds one or more candles in place, also known as a candlestick or candleholder. A candlestand for several candles is called a candelabra. They can be simple or highly ornate, and they can be made of various materials, from wood to brass to silver.  A subtype of candlestick is chamberstick, a short candlestick with a large pan to catch wax and handle, that is used in carrying a candle to the bedroom.
The chandelier originated as a large candlestand designed to be suspended from a ceiling.
The menorah is a candelabra with particular religious significance.

For the Smile Precure! character, see Candy (precure).

rule_evidence.definition:
Also known as Toffee apple, in Commonwealth English.
A whole apple covered in a hard sugar candy coating, caramel, or chocolate. Candy apples are a common treat at autumn festivals such as Halloween.
It is easy to mistake a candy apple for a red lollipop due to artists drawing a candy apple spherical. So take notice of the surroundings, flat bottom/top and size of the candy.

general:captive bead ring.name: captive_bead_ring

rule_evidence.definition:
A ring piercing with a bead that fits into a small opening in the circle of the ring.
The bead is slightly larger than the opening and has small indentations or depressions that correspond to the ring's end-points so that it may fit snugly against them, thus completing the circuit of the ring. Often, a hole is drilled through the bead to allow easier fitting.
Captive bead rings can also have little accessories.

general:chandelier.name: chandelier

rule_evidence.definition:
An ornate lighting fixture that hangs from a ceiling.
Early chandeliers used multiple candles for light, but in modern times these have been replaced with electric lamps. Some chandeliers have arrays of crystal prisms to scatter light throughout a room. Due to their size and the amount of light they produce, chandeliers are usually installed as focal points in large rooms such as dining rooms, lounges, or staircases.
Not to be confused with hanging lights, which are of simple design and only have one or two lamps each, and are often used in kitchens and restaurants.

A device that can be locked onto a person's penis to prevent the wearer from engaging in sexual contact. In many cases, it also makes erection uncomfortable or impossible. Also known as a penis cage. It is used as a sex toy as a method of erotic sexual denial.
Not to be confused with a chastity belt, which serves a similar purpose, but wraps around the wearer's entire waist instead of just the penis. If the "belt" is a strap, band or chain connected to a chastity cage, use chastity cage strap. If it's really a chastity belt that is also a penis cage, use chastity cage-belt.

general:chemical structure.name: chemical_structure

rule_evidence.definition:
A graphical representation of the chemical compound's spatial arrangement of its atoms, molecular shape and often their chemical bonds. It comes in various models and can be either 2D or 3D. Unlike chemical formula which is limited to text.
For example, the chemical structure for water (H₂O) is a basic grid of one hydrogen molecule, one oxygen, and then another hydrogen. More complex substances thus require more complicated grids to outline every molecule present.

general:china dress.meaning_en:
A form-fitting, Chinese dress that has side slits up (usually) both legs and a mandarin collar.
The traditional qipao, also called a cheongsam (Cantonese), was introduced in Qing-era China in the 1600s but did not evolve into its current form until the early 20th century. There are many styles, but it typically is a long, form-fitting dress with a mandarin collar, an asymmetric left-over-right opening, high-to-medium side slits, and embellished with Chinese frog fasteners on the lapel and the collar. It may have any variety of sleeves.

general:chinese hairpin.name: chinese_hairpin

rule_evidence.definition:
An ornate hair stick of Chinese origin.
Prior to the establishment of the Qing dynasty, both men and women coiled their hair into hair buns using a hairpin known as a ji. There were many varieties of hairpin, with different names to denote specific styles, such as zan, ji, chai, buyao and tiaoxin. The materials and design of the hairpins were markers of the wearer's social status. Hairpins could be made out of various materials, such as jade, gold, silver, ivory, bronze, bamboo, carved wood, tortoiseshell and bone.

They are large birds resembling some cross between a chicken and an ostrich or other ratite. Often used as mounts (in the abscence of horses). Primarily yellow, though other colors (and sizes) are known. They make "kweh" and "wark" noises. Baby chocobos are "chicobos" ("ko-chocobos" in Japan). In most games, they are flightless, but other games gave them the ability to fly and swim.
A chibi version heads up the Final Fantasy Fables/Chocobo (series) series.

general:chromatic aberration.name: chromatic_aberration
general:chromatic aberration.explanation_zh: 不同颜色的轮廓略微错位。

rule_evidence.definition:
An effect where the edges of an image have a colored, blurry halo or fringe. The RGB color channels appear noticeably offset from one another.
In photography, chromatic aberration is caused by a defect of the camera lens. The lens refracts light of different wavelengths (colors) slightly differently (technically speaking, the index of refraction of a lens material varies depending on the wavelength), causing the colors to become out of focus.
In digital art, chromatic aberration is used to simulate a photographic look or for artistic effect. In small amounts it can increase realism; in greater
rule_evidence.passage:
An effect where the edges of an image have a colored, blurry halo or fringe. The RGB color channels appear noticeably offset from one another.
In photography, chromatic aberration is caused by a defect of the camera lens. The lens refracts light of different wavelengths (colors) slightly differently (technically speaking, the index of refraction of a lens material varies depending on the wavelength), causing the colors to become out of focus.
In digital art, chromatic aberration is used to simulate a photographic look or for artistic effect. In small amounts it can increase realism; in greater amounts it can create a sense of motion (similar to [[motion blur]]), convey a chaotic environment, or indicate anxiety, paranoia, or mental derangement. In excessive amounts it can induce eyestrain.

general:color timer.name: color_timer

rule_evidence.definition:
A light bulb-like instrument usually attached on an Ultraman's chest. Emitting a steady, blue light at full power, it blinks red if an Ultraman is running out of power or if he is approaching to his time limit. If the Color Timer stops emitting light, it signals either the death of an Ultraman or he'll simply reverts back to his human form. It is also known as the "Warning Light" in the English dub.
Its name differs, depending on which universe, for example; in Gaia's world, it's known as the Life Gauge, or in Nexus' world, it's the Energy Core. And the U40 Ultras instead obtain a similar item

general:corded phone.name: corded_phone

rule_evidence.definition:
A phone with a cord attached to the receiver, as opposed to a cordless phone or modern cellphone.
Corded phones are the oldest of all phones, dominant in everyday use at least until the early 1990s. They may have a rotary dial, although these were gradually superseded by push button systems from the 1980s onward.
The earliest antique phones had no integrated dialing system at all; either the connection was between two devices only, or a manual telephone exchange was needed.

general:corset piercing.name: corset_piercing

rule_evidence.definition:
A type of piercing that consists of multiple piercings in rows, with ribbon, string or chains cross-laced through to mimic the appearance of a corset. Think cross-laced clothes, but directly on the skin instead. Usually a back piercing, though it can be worn elsewhere on the body.
In real life, these piercings are only intended to be temporary; they are rarely worn for more than a week. As such, they're typically done for short-term activites, such as a photo-shoot.
They may also be done as a form of piercing play in BDSM.

The smallest type of couch, one that seats two people, is referred to as a "loveseat."  A couch with a 90 degree bend in it is a "sectional couch," and as the name suggests is composed of several separate sections.
There may be some overlap between a small "loveseat" type couch and a large easy chair. When in doubt, just tag them as a couch.

These illustrations should always be parented or pooled.

general:crossbow.name: crossbow
general:crossbow.meaning_en:
A weapon consisting of a bow (weapon) mounted on a stock that shoots crossbow bolts.
It works in much the same fashion as a regular bow, but replaces manual pulling of the bowstring with the use of a mechanical device, such as a lever or a crank, to draw back the string, allowing for more powerful shots in exchange for being quite slow to load and shoot in comparison to a regular bow.  Crossbows in general are easier to use than regular bows, which require more strength to pull back the bowstring.

general:crosshatching.name: crosshatching

rule_evidence.definition:
A shading technique that uses intersecting lines of varying densities to simulate varying levels of darkness. A lightly colored object will have few lines, whereas a very dark object may have so many lines as to be solid black. Crosshatching is a variant of simple hatching and may have two or more directions in which the lines lie.
This may be used alongside other forms of hatching (texture), such as linear hatching or woven hatching.

rule_evidence.definition:
When characters from unrelated franchises are shown together in the same scene.
Crossover should not be confused with parody. A parody implies mimicking a scene or dialogue from another series, with the intention of being humorous, while a crossover simply implies two characters from different franchises meeting. A character cosplaying as a character from another series also does not normally qualify as a crossover.
See songover for crossovers between multiple songs or other musical compositions, seen commonly with Vocaloid songs.

For tagging purposes this tag is to be used for objects that are generally composed of translucent material and whose surface is composed of facets (flat surfaces).

general:curry rice.name: curry_rice

rule_evidence.definition:
Rice topped with curry. A popular dish in Japan.
The Imperial Japanese Navy adopted curry from the Royal Navy, who adopted it from India, and it became the origin of present Japanese-style curry rice. The Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force's tradition of eating curry rice every Friday lunch originated with the IJN.
Popular toppings for Japanese curry include potatoes, carrots, onions, beef, pork, tonkatsu (food) or chicken (food) katsu, shrimp tempura, sliced boiled egg (food)s, and fukujinzuke.

general:daffodil.name: daffodil

rule_evidence.definition:
Narcissus, commonly called daffodil, is a genus of flowering plants in the family Amaryllidaceae. The scientific name of the plant is often linked to the myth of Narcissus, who became so obsessed with his own reflection in water that he drowned, although it is not clear whether the flower was named after the myth or the myth after the flower. The other common name is jonquil, after a particular species of the family.
Daffodil flowers grow at about a right angle to the stem and have a cup- or trumpet-shaped protruding center surrounded by 6 petal-like tepals (undifferentiated petals and sepals)

Daffodil flowers grow at about a right angle to the stem and have a cup- or trumpet-shaped protruding center surrounded by 6 petal-like tepals (undifferentiated petals and sepals). general:dagger.meaning_en:
A double-edged knife used for stabbing or thrusting. They are often a secondary defense weapon in close combat.
The difference between a dagger and a knife is that daggers are double-edged or edgeless and intended primarily or exclusively for stabbing, while knives are usually single-edged and intended primarily for cutting. Many knives and daggers are capable of either stabbing or cutting.

Should not be confused with quadruple amputee, which will often use the 達磨 tag on pixiv.

general:desert.name: desert
general:desert.meaning_en:
An arid, barren environment. Usually covered in predominantly sand or very loose soil with few animals and plants (e.g. palm trees and cacti) which can survive with very small amounts of water.
Commonly featured in Middle Eastern settings or post-apocalypse fiction to show that resources are scarce or some event has killed most of the life on Earth.
Not to be confused with sweet food items consumed at the end of a meal, known as a dessert.

A donut (also spelled "doughnut") is a small, fried pastry typically glazed with sugar, chocolate, or other frostings. It often contains sweet fillings such as cream, jelly, or custard.
The most common form is the ring-shaped donut, but the term also applies to round, filled donuts and other regional variants. Donuts are popular worldwide and appear frequently in food-related media and illustrations.
In American media, donuts are stereotypically associated with the police, a trope that originated during the interwar period in the United States. Donuts were often the only food readily available

general:dove.name: dove

rule_evidence.definition:
For tagging purposes, this tag refers to the white or mostly white birds, such as the "dove of peace" that is commonly associated with the term "dove."
The term dove is frequently used interchangeably with the term pigeon.  When used more specifically, the term refers to smaller members of the bird family Columbidae, whose members are referred to by either the terms dove or pigeon. Members of this family fall under two major groups based on their diet, with one group predominately eating seeds and the other predominately eating fruits.
Gray or bluish-gray birds should be tagged pigeon instead.

general:duel disk.name: duel_disk

rule_evidence.definition:
A device used for playing Duel Monster card games in the Yu-Gi-Oh! manga and anime. Typically takes the shape of a forearm-mounted contraption with foldable blades that is used to place cards on it. The device utilizes "Solid Vision" technology to generate hologram of monsters and cards played by both players.
In real life, the device was conceived by Takahashi Kazuki as a way to give characters an ability move to more freely during a card game match for dramatic effect instead of having them dueling on a table.

general:duffel bag.name: duffel_bag

rule_evidence.definition:
A duffel bag, also known as a gym bag, is a cylindrical bag carried over the shoulder, made from canvas or similarly rugged materials. It can be closed with a drawstring or zipper. Older military-style designs historically had a single closure on one end; modern variants tend to have zippers along the length of the top and may have multiple compartments for easy storage.
Due to their large size and durability, duffel bags are typically used for hauling sporting equipment and/or uniforms. Travelers may carry them as an alternative to suitcases.

general:duffel coat.name: duffel_coat
general:duffel coat.meaning_en:
A winter coat held shut with toggle-and-loop fasteners. The toggles are cone-like pegs that fit through large loops to hold the coat shut. This design is made to be easy to open and close while wearing gloves in winter.
Duffel coats were originally made from duffel, a thick woolen fabric also used to make duffel bags. The name comes from Duffel, a town in Belgium where the fabric originated.

Acoustic basses feature a larger resonator body to better amplify lower frequencies and a longer neck compared to their acoustic guitar counterparts.

general:electric guitar.name: electric_guitar

rule_evidence.definition:
A guitar that uses a pickup to convert the vibration of its strings into electrical impulses. The most common guitar pickup uses the principle of direct electromagnetic induction. The signal generated by an electric guitar is too weak to drive a loudspeaker, so it is amplified before sending it to a loudspeaker.
Due to the lack of an acoustic resonator, electric guitars are noticeably thinner and come in a much wider variety of shapes and designs than their acoustic counterparts.
This musical instrument is widely used in rock music.

general:emphasis lines.name: emphasis_lines

rule_evidence.definition:
Lines drawn in a burst pattern, radiating outward from a part of the image to which the artist wants to draw attention. They cause the area surrounded by the lines to stand out more in the viewer's eye.
These are not the same as speed lines or motion lines, which indicate fast motion; emphasis lines indicate focus, rather than motion.
A similar technique used in filmography is to focus the camera toward a specific part of the shot (sometimes off-center) while allowing other parts of the image to become unfocused, thus drawing extra attention to the focused area.

general:faceless.name: faceless

rule_evidence.definition:
A character with a defined head whose facial features (mainly the eyes) don't appear, either because they're hidden, covered, in shadow, or not drawn at all.
This is commonly used for characters meant to be viewer self-inserts, or for anonymous background characters (such as crowds of people). It can also be used when a character is extremely embarrassed or flustered, or when a character is completely unamused or has predatory intentions.
If the character literally doesn't have a face (not just due to artistic style or concealed features, e.g. Slender Man), use hole in face, void face, or some

A character with a defined head whose facial features (mainly the eyes) don't appear, either because they're hidden, covered, in [[shadow]], or not drawn at all.
This is commonly used for characters meant to be [[viewer self-insert]]s, or for anonymous background characters (such as [[crowd]]s of [[people]]). It can also be used when a character is extremely [[embarrassed]] or [[flustered]], or when a character is [[completely unamused]] or has predatory intentions.
If the character literally doesn't have a face (not just due to artistic style or concealed features, e.g. [[Slender Man]]), use [[hole in face]], [[void face]], or some combination of [[no eyes]], [[no nose]], or [[no mouth]]. If the character's whole face is shaded but their eyes are still visible, use [[eyes in shadow]] instead.

general:fantasy.name: fantasy

rule_evidence.definition:

Pilots that fly them are equipped with a g-suit and an oxygen mask on their pilot helmet, to allow them to withstand the heavy g-force from maneuvering the aircraft at supersonic speed, and to breathe easily while flying at altitudes of more than 20,000 feet.

general:fighting game.name: fighting_game

rule_evidence.definition:
A video game genre where the player controls an on-screen character and engages in close combat with an opponent. These characters tend to be of equal power and fight matches consisting of several rounds, which take place in an arena (or "stage").
Players must master techniques such as blocking, counter-attacking, and chaining together sequences of attacks known as "combos". Most fighting games allow the player to execute special moves by performing specific command inputs.
Use this tag for artwork referencing fighting gameplay mechanics, such as health bars, character select screens, or VS sc

Compared to more modern soft bulletproof vests or plate carriers with rigid-looking front, flak jackets look more loose-fitting as if it they have soft quilt, having buttoned or zipper front top, collared appearance, and many of them feature pockets or pouc

It should not be used for rear-projection TVs or flat-screen cathode-ray tube TVs, which were particularly common before LCD and similar technologies become the dominate technology used for televisions.

general:flower on head.name: flower_on_head

rule_evidence.definition:
A flower literally growing from the top of a character's head, usually with a stem and a set of leaves. The Pikmin (creature)s from the Pikmin (series) series are examples of this tag.
In anime and manga, a flower growing from a character's head is sometimes an allusion to the Japanese term 脳内お花畑 (nōnai o-hanabatake) - literally "garden in the brain" - meaning that a person is carefree, happy-go-lucky, silly, or stupid. Examples of this include Kaguya in her "bakaguya"/moron mode and Pallas (arknights) from Arknights.
Not to be confused with hair flower, a flower worn in the hair as an ornamen

Examples of this include [[shinomiya_kaguya|Kaguya]] in her "bakaguya"/moron mode and [[Pallas_(arknights)|]] from [[Arknights]].

rule_evidence.definition:
A technique in which an object is depicted at an angle, making it appear shorter than its actual size. This captures the distortion seen when viewing an object at an unusual angle.
Not to be confused with depth of field, which refers to blurry, out-of-focus portions of an image. An image can contain both, but not necessarily.
Poorly done foreshortening may result in bad perspective.

general:forget-me-not (flower).name: forget-me-not_(flower)

rule_evidence.definition:
Myosotis, commonly called forget-me-not or scorpion grass, is a genus of flowering plants in the family Boraginaceae. The type species is Myosotis scorpioides.
Forget-me-nots grow in clusters (cymes). Their five-petaled flowers have a bright, ring-like center that is yellow or white. They are most often blue, but also come in shades of pink, purple, and white.
Not to be confused with tweedia. Tweedia flowers have a similar ring-like center, but it is blue. Also, tweedia flowers grow individually rather than in clusters, and their petals are usually longer.

general:fox.name: fox

Foxes are small-to-medium-sized omnivorous mammals belonging to various genera within the Canidae family, but, strictly speaking, the term refers to the species classified as “true” foxes (genus Vulpes), especially the "red fox" species (Vulpes vulpes).
Foxes are best known for their bushy tails and pointed snouts, as well as their curious and playful behavior.
Foxes are very important to Japanese folklore, being the center of the kitsune myths, often being depicted with multiple tails - up to a total of nine.

general:furry.name: furry

rule_evidence.definition:
An anthropomorphic animal; a character based on an animal but with human traits. Body fur, feathers, or scales are common. Anthro animal characters without body fur, like birds, bugs, and reptiles, still count as furry.
Monster girls or ordinary human characters that only have tails or animal ears are not considered furry.
"Kemono" is the Japanese equivalent of the term "furry", with fans of such being called "kemona" or "kemoner". Just like with furries in the west, there are numerous subcategories and subcultures within.

general:game controller.name: game_controller
general:game controller.meaning_en:
A device used to provide input to a computer or video game. Normally this refers to a controller that is separate from the main machine, connected by wire or wirelessly, as opposed to the controls built into a handheld game console such as a Game Boy or Nintendo DS.
Examples of game controllers include gamepads, joysticks, arcade sticks, steering wheel, light guns, the Microsoft Kinect, and many more.
Gamepads can be held conveniently in two hands and do not require any particular mounting surface nor an exact fixed posture from the user. The gamepad provides basic functions to control a game

general:gas mask.name: gas_mask

rule_evidence.definition:
A full-face mask that protects the wearer from toxic gases and airborne pollutants by covering their nose, mouth, and eyes.
They protect the wearer by forming a sealed cover over the nose and mouth and filters the air that they breath in to prevent inhaling toxic gases or pollutants. The mask also protects the eyes from exposure to toxic gases or pollutants that may cause irritation, temporary blindness, or even permanent eye damage.
If the mask doesn't cover the eyes, then it's a respirator, not a gas mask.

general:gothic lolita.name: gothic_lolita

rule_evidence.definition: Gothic Lolita (ゴスロリ, "GothLoli", or sometimes "Loli-Goth") is a specific kind of fashion that is a mixture of both goth and Lolita fashion. Lolita fashion draws much of its inspiration from Rococo, Victorian-style and Edwardian fashion and often aims to imitate the look of Victorian children or porcelain dolls. general:grenade launcher.name: grenade_launcher

rule_evidence.definition:
A grenade launcher is a weapon that launches a grenade further and more accurately than a soldier could. There are those designed to be attached to long arms and those that are used as standalone weapons. Automatic grenade launchers also exist. These are usually crew-served or mounted on vehicles.
Despite the similarity in names, a grenade launcher is not the same as a rocket propelled grenade launcher and they should not be tagged as such.

general:greyscale.name: greyscale
general:greyscale.meaning_en:
A completely colorless, black-and-white image. The image is composed exclusively of shades of black, white, and grey. It is very common for comics and doujinshi to be in greyscale.
The image may have small highlights of color (known as spot colors), but the image as a whole should be predominately greyscale.
Don't use color tags like black eyes or black hair when tagging greyscale images. The exception is color background tags, so tagging white background, grey background, or black background is fine.

general:greyscale with colored backgroun.name: greyscale_with_colored_background

rule_evidence.definition:
A common composition where a greyscale subject is on a colored background, usually also a simple background.
Do not tag these as greyscale, partially colored or spot color.
If small parts of the subject, not part of the background, are colored, such as the subject's eyes, spot color can be used. If the subject has enough coloring that you'd tag it partially colored, use partially colored instead and do not use this tag.

general:grid background.name: grid_background

rule_evidence.definition:
A typically single-color background formed into a square grid by a series of thin lines.
The lines must be perpendicular or parallel with respect to each other, but not necessarily to the sides of the image; a square grid that has been rotated is still a square grid.
Not to be confused with checkered background, where the squares contain two alternating colors, or border, a line that runs along three to four edges of the image.

Do not tag bass guitars as regular guitars. A bass guitar has four strings, while a regular guitar has six.

general:gyaru v.name: gyaru_v

rule.phrase: an upside-down V sign with the palm facing out

rule_evidence.definition:
An upside-down V gesture, with the V pointing down and the palm facing out.
The gesture originates from Japan's Gyaru culture. The original term is called "Gyaru-peace", which is a combination of the Japanese pronunciation of "Gal," an English slang for women and girls, and the English word "Peace," which means the finger gesture V.

A gym, or gymnasium is an athletic facility equipped for physical training, weight lifting, and sport.

For the room that stores a gym's equipment, see gym storeroom. See gymnastics for the alternate shortening for gym.

Another common type of hachimaki has a rising sun emblem like the Japanese flag, or a short inspirational slogan meant to be displayed across the forehead.

general:hagoromo.name: hagoromo

rule_evidence.definition:
A hagoromo (羽衣, lit. "Feather Robe") is a long, thin shawl depicted as the mythical of tennin (天人) in Japanese mythology. Its visual form is based on the Chinese pibo (披帛), a light silk scarf worn by women in ancient China, particularly during the Tang dynasty.
The concept of celestial beings wearing flowing, floating shawls originated in Chinese folklore. The earliest known "feather robe" tale appears in the 4th-century text Soushen Ji (搜神记), and the motif appears in the legend of the Cowherd and Weaver Girl (牛郎织女) and the myth of the Seven Fairy Maidens (七仙女). This motif later spread to Japa

general:hair bobbles.name: hair_bobbles

rule_evidence.definition:

Stereotypically associated with young or teenage girls.
Not to be confused with hair beads. Hair beads usually consist of many smaller beads and aren't always used to tie the hair. Hair bobbles usually consist of two larger beads normally used to tie the hair.

Hair sticks are extremely old and can be traced back to ancient China, Egypt, Greece and India. They can be as simple as a literal stick or branch, or highly intricate with lots of detail.

general:hakama.name: hakama
general:hakama.meaning_en:
Traditional Japanese clothing, looking like either a pleated skirt (a hakama skirt) or baggy, pleated pants (hakama pants). A traditional hakama has seven deep pleats, five in the front and two in the rear.
Hakama are split into a front and back section at the top, which are tied at the waist, often with visible hip vents and usually covering the midriff. Hakama are normally worn over a kimono and are very often red in color, although any color may be used. Traditional hakama are long garments, but non-traditional hakama short skirts and hakama shorts are often seen in anime.

general:halberd.name: halberd
general:halberd.meaning_en:
A polearm with a head consisting of an axe blade, a spearhead, and a hook or angled spike opposite the axe.
While the term halberd refers specifically to the medieval/renaissance European polearm, similar polearms such as the knightly poleaxe/pollaxe and Chinese qinglong ji also fall under this category.

general:half crown braid.name: half_crown_braid

rule_evidence.definition: A crown braid that is only braided on one side of the head or without a braid at the top. If both sides and the top of the head are braided, use crown braid instead.

general:half crown braid.meaning_en: A crown braid that is only braided on one side of the head or without a braid at the top. If both sides and the top of the head are braided, use crown braid instead.

general:half gloves.name: half_gloves
general:half gloves.meaning_en:
A type of short glove that doesn't cover the wrists.
Not to be confused with fingerless gloves, which cover the wrists but not the fingers.

general:half mask.name: half_mask

rule_evidence.definition:

For half masks that only cover the mouth and jaw, use mouth mask instead. For half masks that only go over one eye, use half eye mask instead. For half masks that only cover one eye, use half blindfold mask instead.

If there's a visible tail hanging from the center of the loop, use half up half down braid instead. If the braid goes around the top of the head, use crown braid instead. If the braid goes around the nape, use nape braid instead.

general:half updo.name: half_updo
general:half updo.explanation_zh: 只将上半部分头发扎起。

Use one side up if the hair is tied on the side instead of the back.

general:half-closed eye.name: half-closed_eye

rule_evidence.definition: A single eye partially closed, while the other eye is fully open or closed. Also applicable if you see the half-closed eye, but the other eye is covered by something like hair, an eyepatch, a hat, or something else. It's also possible the character only has one eye.

general:half-skirt.name: half-skirt

rule_evidence.definition:

Not to be confused with a showgirl skirt, in which the entire front area is missing, or with a high-low skirt in which the front half is shorter than the back.

general:halftone.name: halftone

rule_evidence.definition:
A technique in which small dots of varying size and shape are used to simulate different tones of color or shades of grey. This can be either as an artistic choice, or as a printing technique to simulate smooth gradients using a single color of ink. At a distance, the dots will appear to blend together and produce a smooth gradient.
If the dots are all equal in size, use Ben-Day dots instead.

general:hamburger steak.name: hamburger_steak

rule_evidence.definition:
A food item which consists of ground meat clumped together in a round shape and cooked. Unlike a meatloaf, neither a mold nor oven are used, and it is mainly cooked on a frying pan.
Although it is known by several names, such as "hamburger patty" or "salisbury steak", in Japan it is called either "hamburg" (ハンバーグ) or "hamburg steak" (ハンバーグステーキ). Moreover, just like its name, this dish's ingredients and seasonings all vary slightly.
In Japan, it is extremely popular among children, and is a standard part of the menu in school lunches and family restaurants.

general:hammer.meaning_en: A tool or weapon meant to deliver an impact to an object. The most common uses are for driving nail (hardware)s in construction, fitting parts, forging metal, and breaking up objects. A large hammer, such as sledgehammer, can be used as a deadly bludgeoning weapon.

general:hammer and sickle.name: hammer_and_sickle

rule_evidence.definition:
The hammer and sickle is a part of communist symbolism and its usage indicates an association with Communism, a Communist party, or a Communist state. It symbolizes the unity of peasants and workers.
Although it is a universal symbol for communism, it is typically associated with the Soviet Union due to being the first country that adopted the symbol.
Nowadays the usage of the Hammer and Sickle has been banned in certain Nations, only the use of it is allowed in arts.

general:han'eri.name: han'eri

rule_evidence.definition:
A decorative piece of cloth worn under the neckline of a kimono to add style or color to an outfit. Recognizable by the kimono's neckline contrasting in color or design with the rest of the kimono.
Often embroidered with flower motifs or geometric designs. Can be made of polyester, crepe, satin, linen, leno weave gauze, or Shioze silk. There are some unusual han'eri where the design embroidered on each side is different.
Technically, the han'eri is sewn to the collar of the juban, the undergarment worn beneath the kimono.

general:hanbok.name: hanbok

rule_evidence.definition:
Traditional Korean clothing. It is often characterized by vibrant colors and simple lines without pockets. It consists of a bolero-like jacket called a jeogori (clothes) and either roomy pants bound at the ankles (baji) for men, or a long skirt (chima (clothes)) for women. A hat called a gat is also common.
Hanbok has a long history dating back to the Three Kingdoms period (c. 1st century BCE – 7th century CE) and has independently evolved over centuries.

general:handgun.name: handgun

rule_evidence.definition:
A short-barrelled firearm designed to be used with one hand or two hands and for shooting at short-ranged targets, while be more concealable to be holstered than a rifle or a submachine gun. Its ammunition feeding mechanism may vary by design, such as muzzle-loading earlier handguns, break action, by using clips or more commonly magazines.
Handgun types include modern semi-automatic pistols, revolvers, antique firearms such as flintlocks and derringers. This tag also covers the "machine pistol", a handgun capable of fully automatic fire (e.g. Beretta 93R).
The term "pistol" refers to handguns

Its [[ammunition]] feeding mechanism may vary by design, such as muzzle-loading earlier handguns, [[break action]], by using [[clip (weapon)|clips]] or more commonly [[magazine (weapon)|magazines]].
Handgun types include modern semi-automatic pistols, [[revolver]]s, [[antique firearm]]s such as [[flintlock]]s and [[derringer]]s. This tag also covers the "machine pistol", a handgun capable of fully automatic fire (e.g. [[Beretta 93R]]).
The term "pistol" refers to handguns with a single, stationary (non-revolving) chamber.  In Danbooru, the "pistol" tag redirects to the "handgun" tag.

Males' hair may be pulled back into a simple ponytail or bun or held by a coronet. Emperors or princes may wear mian guan. If nothing else, huadian (forehead mark), or the circular fan is an easy distinguishing mark.
Hanfu differs from the Qing-era clothing of the mid-1600

general:haori.name: haori
general:haori.meaning_en:
A wide-sleeved silk jacket worn over a kimono. Mostly worn by men, this jacket is at hip- or thigh-length. There may be a decorative tie string called haori himo across the chest or the middle of the jacket.
Shinsengumi are identified by a light blue haori, with sleeves trimmed with white dandara-moyou (mountain stripes).
Not to be confused with kataginu, which more resembles a vest than a traditional jacket, or with happi, which has tube-sleeves, instead of kimono sleeves.

general:happi.name: happi
general:happi.meaning_en:
A traditional Japanese tube/straight-sleeved jacket worn during festivals. Has a thick border (usually black in color) running down the coat opening, with the jacket length usually reaching between the hips and waist. The happi may be worn open or fastened closed with the use of a cloth belt. The sleeves are usually on the shorter side, but can also reach the wrists.
Traditionally indigo or brown in color, though other colors exist.
For a type of traditional indoor winter jacket, use hanten (clothes).

rule_evidence.definition:
A display device which completely covers the eyes and is not transparent. It doesn't need to be used for virtual reality, but odds are that the visor displays some sort of visual or tactical image to the user.
Often used by characters in science fiction settings, or for characters wearing VR headsets.

general:headband.name: headband
general:headband.meaning_en:
A strap worn across the forehead, such as a sweatband, a strip of cloth worn during martial arts or athletic events, or a piece of ninja armor (however apocryphal).
While a headband may be used to keep hair out of the eyes, it is usually worn under at least part of the hair. Headbands often end with a long tail trailing behind the head where they are tied.
Not to be confused with hairband, which is a band worn on top of the head instead of on the forehead, and is used to hold the hair down to maintain a hairstyle.

general:headdress.name: headdress

rule_evidence.definition:
An ornamental covering or band for the head, especially one worn on ceremonial occasions.
Use this tag for ornamental headdresses, such as the Native American headdress. Most headgear that can be described as "hairband but with lots of rigid(ish) decorations attached" or "hat/bonnet but truncated to only the middle 'band' part" are generally headdresses.
This tag can also be used as a fallback tag for ornamental headgear in general, but try to avoid using this tag for hats, helmets, hair ornaments, headbands, fake animal ears and simple ribbons.

general:hime cut.explanation_zh: 齐刘海与脸侧整齐截断的发束，后侧可保留长发。
general:hime cut.meaning_en:
A hairstyle consisting of long straight hair, blunt bangs, and sidelocks with blunt ends.
All elements must be present to be considered a hime cut. The hair must be long and straight and the bangs and sidelocks must have blunt ends. Tied hair, such as ponytails, twintails, braids, hair buns, hair rings, does not count.
As the name suggests, the style is thought to have originated, or at least become common, in the Imperial court during the Heian period of Japanese history, when noble women would sometimes grow out their hair for their entire lives.

Back in the late 19th century, when Hogwarts Legacy happens, the uniform had plaid pants for the boys and long plaid skirts for the girls.

Don't use for holding body parts (like [[holding hands]], or holding someone's breasts, or [[holding own hair]] - unless it's [[holding detached hair]]) or for holding clothing being worn (like [[holding own skirt]]), or for holding things with something other than the hands (like a [[mouth hold]], [[holding with feet]], or [[holding with tail]]).
To search for something specific being held, search [code]holding_<name of object>[/code]. If that fails, use two tags together, like this: {{holding mimikaki}}.

rule_evidence.definition:
A character is holding any sort of long polearm behind their back, rather than in front of them. The 'polearm' in question can be anything like a spear, staff, broom, rod, or such. This tag basically encompasses the variety of postures that characters can utilize to accomplish this.
Note that this tag refers to when a polearm is actually being held in the character's hands. If it's strapped to their back, planted in the ground behind them, or they're otherwise not holding it, don't use this tag.

general:hololive dance practice uniform.name: hololive_dance_practice_uniform

rule_evidence.definition:
An official costume of hololive members, first appeared on November 13, 2023 during the Hoshimatic Project training stream.
It consists of a white cropped t-shirt with a black stripe across the arms and hemline with "HOLOLIVE" and the the name of the wearer on it, and a visible overhang revealing a black sports bra underneath,   and either black yoga pants/sweatpants or black shorts.
The outfit also has slight variations between each member, with the most notable one being Hoshimachi Suisei's featuring a black leotard underneath.

general:homu.name: homu

rule_evidence.definition:
A sound effect associated with Akemi Homura from Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica. A play off her name in a similar manner to Pokémon. Homura's nickname among Japanese fans is Homuhomu. This phrase was never used in the drama, though.

general:honey.name: honey

rule_evidence.definition:
A sweet substance that is exclusively produced by honey bees using nectar from flowers. It is widely used for sweetening foods, for flavoring, and for medicinal properties.
Honey is one of the few foods in the world that in its raw state will never spoil if properly stored, this is due to honey's low water content, high acidity, and it containing small amounts hydrogen peroxide.

general:honey.meaning_en:
A sweet substance that is exclusively produced by honey bees using nectar from flowers. It is widely used for sweetening foods, for flavoring, and for medicinal properties.
Honey is one of the few foods in the world that in its raw state will never spoil if properly stored, this is due to honey's low water content, high acidity, and it containing small amounts hydrogen peroxide.

general:horizon.name: horizon

rule_evidence.definition:
The horizon is the border between earth (planet) and sky. As the horizon is usually obscured by trees, mountains, buildings, etc., it is most visible in settings dominated by the ocean or other featureless terrain.
When the outline of a city is visible over the horizon, this is known as a skyline.
If the horizon is tilted with respect to the picture frame, the result is a dutch angle.

rule_evidence.definition:
A type of uniformed clothing provided by hospitals for patients, also know as a patient gown. There're mainly two variants. The loose detachable robe for patients undergoing operations or examinations. The pajamas-like buttoned top-and-bottom set for hospitalized patients, often vertically striped. Their designs are not very standardized, versions often vary in details. The most common colors are blue and white, pink is also somewhat common.
Patients can often be seen with an iv stand and an intravenous drip.
Not to be confused with medical scrubs, a type of medical gown for medical workers du

general:hydrangea.name: hydrangea

rule_evidence.definition:
A genus of flowering plants of the Hydrangeaceae family, native to southern and eastern Asia. Most species are shrubs, but some are small trees. Commonly called hortensia.
Hydrangeas bear globular or umbrella-shaped clusters of flowers that come out any time from early spring to late autumn in a variety of colors influenced by the pH level of the soil. Commonly depicted in shades of blue, purple, and pink.
In Japan, it is commonly associated with the rainy season. Its Japanese name is "ajisai" (アジサイ or 紫陽花), which refers specifically to Hydrangea macrophylla, the bigleaf hydrangea.

general:indian style.name: indian_style
general:indian style.meaning_en:
Sitting with the butt on the ground and the legs crossed at the ankles, pretzel style. Also known as sitting cross-legged in English, as tailor style or Turkish style in several European languages, and as agura (胡坐) in Japanese, where it is the traditional informal male sitting style.

Do not confuse this tag for Indian-styled clothing. Those are tagged as Asian Indian clothes.

general:innertube.name: innertube

rule_evidence.definition:

They are filled with air and worn around the torso or sat on while floating on the water. They are often constructed of transparent material, ostensibly for better visibility of the wearer.

general:instant noodles.name: instant_noodles

rule_evidence.definition:

The instant noodle block is generally sold in two sorts of packaging, instant pack noodles (generally in square packs, sometimes sold in bulk) or instant cup noodles (generally sold in a cup- or bowl-shaped container).

general:iron cross.name: iron_cross

rule_evidence.definition:
The Iron Cross (Eiserne Kreuz) is a German military symbol and medal, consisting of a black cross pattée with a white outline. It has been used by Kingdom of Prussia, the German Empire (1871-1918), Nazi Germany (1933-1945), and by the Bundeswehr (the modern German armed forces) since 1956.
Some video games, such as World War II-themed shooters, Kantai Collection, and Azur Lane, use Iron Crosses to as a substitute for the swastika in order to comply with censorship laws and avoid offending their audience with Nazi symbols.
For similar cross symbols that lack an outline and are used outside Germ

general:isometric.name: isometric

rule_evidence.definition:
A method of representing a 3D object on a 2D plane used in technical and engineering drawings. Unlike in perspective drawings or real life, parallel lines do not converge to a vanishing point and objects appear to be the same size regardless of distance.
Note that this tag refers to what is technically called axonometric projection of which isometric projection is a special case. Consequently, many images tagged as isometric on Danbooru may actually be dimetric or trimetric.

general:jack-o'-lantern.name: jack-o'-lantern

rule_evidence.definition:
A vegetable lantern commonly carved from a pumpkin, typically as a Halloween decoration. The pumpkin has a face or image carved into it, and the insides are usually scooped out so that a candle can be placed inside to illuminate the carving.
The practice originated from Ireland where they would use turnips or mangelwurzel to craft these lanterns for Halloween.  Irish immigrants brought this tradition to North America where it led to the development of carving pumpkins to make jack-o'-lanterns.

general:jiangshi.name: jiangshi

rule_evidence.definition:
A Chinese undead. Often called a "Chinese hopping vampire".
They drain people's life energy, hence the "vampire" denomination, although they are more similar in concept to Western zombies.
They usually have fulu or ofuda (strips of paper) stuck to their foreheads and their arms outstretched in a zombie pose. Modern iterations are often seen wearing a rimmed round hat known as a qingdai guanmao, referencing how Chinese officials under the Qing Empire were viewed as bloodthirsty creatures with little regard for humanity.

general:kanji.name: kanji

rule_evidence.definition:
Kanji (漢字) are Chinese characters that are used in the modern Japanese writing system along with hiragana and katakana. Included in Kanji are Kokuji (国字), which are Japanese-made Chinese characters, Ryakuji (略字), which are Japanese colloquial simplifications, and most importantly, Shinjitai (新字体), which serve as a domestic equivalent to Simplified Chinese characters, whose simplifications can differ from their Chinese counterparts (contrasted by Kyuujitai , equivalent to Traditional Chinese characters).
Since almost all Japanese text will have kanji, this tag is useless.

A type of Japanese sword, often called a "samurai sword" because of its historical associations with feudal-era Japan.

general:kikkoumon.name: kikkoumon

rule_evidence.definition:
A hexagon pattern used in traditional Japanese art. Literally "tortoise shell design". Kikkoumon are used in family crests as well as repeated in different combinations to form various patterns.
Kikkoumon can be distinguished from similar patterns like a honeycomb background in that they often have multiple thick borders, and may have flowers or other traditional motifs inside of them.
An alternate version may resemble intersecting or interwoven three-pointed shapes.

general:kimono.name: kimono
general:kimono.meaning_en:
A type of traditional Japanese clothing, consisting of a long, wide-sleeved robe, closed at the front forming a "y" shape. It is held closed with a wide belt-like sash called an obi. The sleeves can be tied back with tasuki.
Kimonos are often worn with other traditional accessories, such as zouri (traditional wooden sandals), tabi (split-toe socks), and kanzashi (traditional hair ornaments). A kinchaku (small cloth drawstring bag) is often carried while wearing a kimono.
Kimonos come in many different styles for different occasions. Yukata are worn during summer to summer festivals or to onsen

general:kitchen.name: kitchen
general:kitchen.meaning_en:
A room used for cooking in a house or commercial establishment, such as a restaurant.
Home kitchens usually contain a refrigerator, an oven or stove, cupboards, cabinets, counters, a sink, and sometimes a table. Professional kitchens may contain stainless steel working tables, larger sinks, and numerous cooking pots, pans, and utensils. Depending on the establishment, there may be different appliances such as a grill, a rotisserie, a pizza oven, and so forth.
A kitchen designed around baking breads and confections is called a bakery.

A kitsune with all nine tails is a kyuubi.

A type of traditional Japanese clothing, consisting of a long, wide-sleeved robe, closed at the front forming a "y" shape. It is held closed with a wide belt-like sash called an obi. The sleeves can be tied back with tasuki.
Kimonos are often worn with other traditional accessories, such as zouri (traditional wooden sandals), tabi (split-toe socks), and kanzashi (traditional hair ornaments). A kinchaku (small cloth drawstring bag) is often carried while wearing a kimono.
Kimonos come in many different styles for different occasions. Yukata are worn during summer to summer festivals or to onsen

general:kyuubi.name: kyuubi

rule_evidence.definition:
A fox (or fox girl) with nine tails.
The nine-tailed fox is a mythical creature that originated in Chinese mythology, where it is known as huli jing (fox spirit) or jiuweihu (nine-tailed fox). The concept later spread to Korea (as kumiho) and then to Japan (as kyuubi or kyuubi no kitsune).
In Japanese mythology, the kyuubi is stated to be the pinnacle of age and power for a kitsune, taking at least 800 years to attain (100 years per tail). Kyuubi are supposedly near‑godlike in power.

general:lance.name: lance
general:lance.meaning_en:
A type of polearm, traditionally used by cavalry or in jousting, which has a distinct and large cone for its head intended to maximize the thrusting power on impact. The cone can be as long as, or even longer, than the actual haft. Lances are a popular symbol for a knight.
Not to be confused with "lances" in Fire Emblem games, which improperly use the term to refer to any kind of spear, or "lance (senjou no valkyria)s" in Valkyria Chronicles, which are a line of rocket launchers.

general:leather.name: leather

rule_evidence.definition:
A durable and flexible material created via the tanning of hides.
In appearance, it is often vaguely similar to latex, but with the softer shine and higher value range that come with more spread out light reflection, a distinguished pattern, and less skin-tight. The pattern is not a requirement however, and won't be visible in most images on danbooru anyway. Likewise, it will often be drawn more skin-tight than expected.
There are various forms of leather, including ones with plastic finishes, making distinguishing between leather and latex rather hard at times, especially in anime-style art.

general:leotard.name: leotard
general:leotard.meaning_en:
A skin tight, one-piece garment that covers the torso but leaves the legs free.
Leotards usually lack sleeves and are often strapless, though sleeved varieties do exist. Most leotards sport a very simple design, and are typically made of light fabrics to accommodate athletic activities. They are generally worn by athletes such as gymnasts, ballerinas, dancers, and circus performers.
If the garment covers the legs even partially, it's a unitard. If it covers both the arms and the legs, it may be a bodysuit.

general:letterman jacket.name: letterman_jacket

rule_evidence.definition:

Letterman jackets commonly have a large letter (hence "letter"man) on one side on the jackets chest, indicating typically the name of a school or team. The sleeves are often a different color from the jackets body. The jackets collar is often also horizontally striped.

general:lifebuoy.name: lifebuoy

rule_evidence.definition:
A type of swim ring designed to be thrown to a person in the water to prevent drowning.
It differs from an innertube because it is often made of solid buoyant material (rather than being air-filled), and is usually orange or red-and-white in color to maximize visibility in the water. It also may have a line to pull the person holding onto it.
The term "life buoy" is most common in British English. In American English these are better known as "life preservers".

general:light machine gun.name: light_machine_gun

rule_evidence.definition:
A type of machine gun designed to be operated by a single person, with or without an assistant.
Early LMG designs were typically magazine-fed and they fire full-powered rifle cartridge, such as the .303 British Bren. Modern post-World War II designs fire intermediate round, and they can be either belt-fed or magazine-fed (e.g. the 5.56×45mm NATO M249 saw). They are also known as the squad automatic weapon.
Some LMGs are based on the existing service (assault) rifle, such as the RPK.

They are also known as the [i]squad automatic weapon[/i].

general:lily (flower).name: lily_(flower)

rule_evidence.definition:
A flower of the genus Lilium in the family Liliaceae.
Lily flowers have 6 petals (technically 3 petals and 3 sepals) and come in a variety of shapes such as bell, flat, funnel, recurved, trumpet, etc. They can be almost any color, but white lilies are probably the most well-known kind, being either Lilium candidum (Madonna Lilies) or Lilium longiflorum (Easter Lily) with their characteristic trumpet shape.
Lilies are a symbol for Girls Love as well as an eponym for its alternate name yuri due to their Japanese name "yuri".

general:limiter (tsukumo sana).name: limiter_(tsukumo_sana)

rule_evidence.definition:
An accessory for hololive EN VTuber Tsukumo Sana, who almost always wears it on her head like an ahoge. It's a thin, light-purple piece of material that sticks out from the top of the head and then spirals outward, similar to a mosquito coil. If a post clearly shows Sana not wearing her limiter, it's probably a case of the no headgear tag.
Lore-wise, it's meant to shrink her down to a size where she can safely interact with humans, since her true form is almost 1.7 billion metres tall and would make it impossible for her to be anywhere near Earth (which is only about 12.7 million metres wide)

general:lobster.name: lobster

rule_evidence.definition:
A large marine crustacean with stalked eyes, long antennae, and five pairs of legs, the first pair of which are large pincer claws.
A lobster's flesh is considered a delicacy in many countries. It can be boiled and eaten straight, or incorporated into a number of recipes.

rule_evidence.passage:

The fashion consists primarily of a knee length [[skirt]] or [[dress]], [[headdress]], [[blouse]], [[petticoat]]/[[crinoline]], [[kneehighs|knee length socks]] or [[thighhighs|stockings]] and [[rocking horse shoes]], [[high heels]] or [[mary janes]]. general:looking at self.name: looking_at_self

rule_evidence.definition: This tag indicates a character is generally looking at themselves. For example this applies when a character looks at their own body (such as when dressing or checking out an outfit), or at their own reflection in a mirror (provided both they and the reflection are visible to the viewer and the reflection matches reality).  Use looking at hand or  looking at hands when a character is specifically looking only at their hand(s), looking at mirror when a mirror reflection is involved, or looking at another when the "self" is actually another iteration of dual persona or multiple persona.

general:looking at viewer.name: looking_at_viewer
general:looking at viewer.explanation_zh: 人物视线朝向画面外的观看者。
general:looking at viewer.meaning_en:
A character looking directly at the viewer, i.e. looking at the camera or through the fourth wall.
Don't confuse with eye contact, which is for characters making eye contact with each other.
Don't confuse with facing viewer, which should be used when the eyes are closed, covered (e.g. with a blindfold), or looking at another direction.

general:looking away.name: looking_away
general:looking away.meaning_en: Ambiguous. If the character is deliberately looking away from the viewer or character(s) out of a certain emotion, use averting eyes. If the character is simply not looking at the viewer, use one of the tags that indicates looking direction listed below. If the character is angling their body in some way relative to the viewer or character(s), but has eyes closed or obstructed, use one of the tags that indicates facing direction listed below.

general:looking back.name: looking_back
general:looking back.meaning_en:
A character turning their head, body or eyes to look behind themselves.
The subject's gaze should be directed fully or almost fully backwards over the shoulder, anywhere from 135 to 180 degrees behind them relative to their front.
Oftentimes combined with from behind and looking at viewer, and also sideways glance if the character's body is partly facing away.

general:looking down.name: looking_down
general:looking down.meaning_en:
Looking down, with the head bent down. See downturned eyes for when the eyes are looking down but the head is not bent down.
Not to be confused when a character is "figuratively" looking down on others. If that's the case, apply the tag disgust instead.

general:looking through legs.name: looking_through_legs

rule_evidence.definition:
Looking at the viewer through one's own legs. Frequently seen when a character is standing up, with their head and torso fully bent in half in a frontbend so they are looking behind them upside-down.
This is not the same as view between legs since that tag refers to the viewer's perspective. This tag refers to the character's perspective.

[[looking at viewer|Looking at the viewer]] through one's own legs. Frequently seen when a character is [[standing]] up, with their head and torso fully bent in half in a [[frontbend]] so they are looking behind them [[upside-down]].
This is not the same as [[view between legs]] since that tag refers to the viewer's perspective. This tag refers to the character's perspective.

general:looking to the side.name: looking_to_the_side
general:looking to the side.meaning_en:
When a character's gaze is directed to something off to their side. This is most often eyes looking 90 degrees across the shoulder, but eyes looking up to 45 degrees in either direction from the shoulder are also included.
Looking to the side is relative to the character's front, not the viewer's perspective. If the eyes are directed more than 45 degrees backwards use looking back instead.
If the character looks to the side without moving their head, combine with sideways glance. Not to be confused with averting eyes, where someone deliberately diverts their gaze from the viewer/others out of

general:looking up.name: looking_up
general:looking up.meaning_en:

See upturned eyes for when the eyes are looking up but the head is not bent back, or facing up when the eyes are closed.

general:loose belt.name: loose_belt
general:loose belt.meaning_en:
A belt worn loosely, as an accessory, rather than to hold up another piece of clothing.
Use open belt for an unbuckled belt.

general:loose bowtie.name: loose_bowtie
general:loose bowtie.meaning_en:
A loose bowtie is a bowtie that is still tied, but is distinctly loosened around the wearer's neck. A common feature of school uniforms in gyaru fashion.
If it is full undone, use undone bowtie instead.

general:loose hair strand.name: loose_hair_strand
general:loose hair strand.meaning_en:
Single strands of hair that are drawn out of place, separated from the rest of the hair.
Sometimes, this is an element of messy hair or floating hair where a clean hairstyle is disrupted, but can also appear on the periphery of otherwise orderly hair, or in front of a character's face, as with many cases where a strand of hair is stuck to one's mouth, or ahead of the bulk of the hair as a distinct loose stroke.
Note that this tag is only for single strands of hair, these will be usually drawn in a single stroke, either in black, white, or a shade of the color of the hair.  It is not for bundle

general:loose neck ribbon.name: loose_neck_ribbon
general:loose neck ribbon.meaning_en:
When a neck ribbon is tied but hangs loosely around a character's neck and/or shoulders.
When a neck ribbon is untied but still hanging around the wearer's neck, tag with undone neck ribbon instead.

general:loose necktie.name: loose_necktie
general:loose necktie.meaning_en:
