When a tie is untied but still hanging around the wearer's neck, tag with undone necktie instead.

general:loose shirt.name: loose_shirt
general:loose shirt.meaning_en: A shirt that hangs just loosely off the wearer's body, but isn't blatantly too large for them as with oversized shirt.

general:loose socks.name: loose_socks
general:loose socks.meaning_en:
Socks that are loose and baggy, usually worn bunched below the knee. Mainly come in white and seen most often with school uniforms. They are commonly associated with gyaru and kogal fashion.
Not to be confused with leg warmers, which are similarly baggy but don't cover the feet.

general:loose thighhigh.name: loose_thighhigh

rule_evidence.definition:
When a character is wearing thighhighs, and one of them has been loosened or fallen down. This can be a quirk of fashion sense, or mere accident.
Not to be confused with loose socks, which are a specific paired item of clothing.

general:lord camelot (fate).name: lord_camelot_(fate)

rule_evidence.definition:
Mash Kyrielight's and by extension Galahad (fate)'s large black shield, made from the Round Table of Camelot where the Knights of the Round Table (fate) would sit. It is capable of repelling attacks, so long as the user's willpower doesn't falter. It also grants its user and Master an anti-poison ward, and is the catalyst used for summoning Servants in Fate/Grand Order. In the Olympus Lostbelt, it gains an additional cannon-like weapon called the Black Barrel (type-moon), which is capable of destroying gods.
It was originally designed to be Tachie (fate)'s shield, but her character was scrappe

general:lotus.name: lotus

rule_evidence.definition:
An aquatic plant belonging to the Nelumbonaceae family of flowering plants. The lotus has prominent blooms (of pink or white hues) rising 8-12 inches above the water, each with a flattened central seed pod structure and fully circular leaves with centrally-attached stems. These features help distinguish it from the water lily flower (Nymphaea), with which it is often confused.
Nelumbo nucifera (also known as the Sacred or Indian Lotus) will probably be the plant of interest to Danbooru image taggers, being a divine symbol in Hinduism and Buddhism. It conveys the virtues of purity and non-attac

general:lotus leaf.name: lotus_leaf

rule_evidence.definition:
A round leaf of the Nelumbo family (lotuses).
Young lotus leaves float on the surface of the water, but they rise above it as they mature. They have no notches unless they are damaged, which helps distinguish them from lily pads, which float on the water's surface and have a single notch in each leaf.
Because of their hydrophobic surface, lotus leaves are often depicted with water drops on them.

general:lounge chair.name: lounge_chair

rule_evidence.definition:
A type of outdoor chair that allows a sunbather to recline in a relaxed position. Often found at a beach or at poolside, possibly in conjunction with a parasol. Also known as a sun lounger, chaise lounge (US), or deck chair (UK).
They serve a similar purpose as a deck chair, though a deck chair is a type of folding chair (with a fabric or vinyl strip that forms the seat and backrest) and the shapes are reversed. A sun lounger has a longer seat than back, while a deck chair has a longer back than seat.

rule_evidence.definition:

Common scenes include an exterior view of a hotel with a suggestive name on a sign (like 休憩 ¥XXXX), characters implying or mentioning that they're going to a love hotel, suggestive elements inside the room such as a heart bed, sex toys on the nightstand, hotel-issued condoms in a small container near the bed, etc.
Combine with hotel room if the scene takes place inside the room itself.

general:m1911.name: m1911

rule_evidence.definition:
An American single-action, semi-automatic handgun designed by John Moses Browning. Its short-recoil operation with a reciprocating slide highly influenced modern pistol designs.
The M1911 is visually identifiable by its external hammer, a beaver tail safety, both grip panels being held by two screws and a thumb safety. Chambered for the .45 ACP handgun cartridge, the standard magazine (weapon) capacity is seven rounds. In 1924, the M1911 was largely revised into the M1911A1, with a shorter trigger and a longer back spur. It was the standard sidearm of the U.S. military from 1911 to 1985.

Often made of jade (gemstone), magatama were produced in prehistoric Japan, and are associated with ancient Japanese mythology. Similar jewels were found in ancient Korea, where they are called gogok
A famous example is the Yasakani no Magatama, one of the three imperial regalia of Japan.

general:magazine (weapon).name: magazine_(weapon)

rule_evidence.definition:
A device used for storing ammunition and feeding it into a repeating firearm. May be referred to as a "mag" for short. Found in internal as well as external types, the most common is the detachable box magazine, such as that used by most modern assault rifles and semi-automatic handguns. Magazines generally have spring-like object inside that pushes ammunition into the chamber.
Not to be confused with a clip (weapon), a simple strip that store multiple rounds together as a unit for reloading into the fixed magazine or cylinder of a firearm.

general:meiji schoolgirl uniform.name: meiji_schoolgirl_uniform

rule_evidence.definition:
A traditional women's outfit from turn-of-the-century Japan. It typically consists of a kimono (often with simple decorative patterns), a hakama skirt worn over it at the waist, and high laced boots, sometimes with a hair bow.
In the later years of the Meiji Era, the Japanese government began to encourage the establishment of women's junior high schools. Typical Japanese women's clothing at the time, however, was more showy and elaborate than modest or functional. As a result, this style quickly rose in popularity as a more practical alternative for women attending school. Even in the present

In the later years of the [[Meiji]] Era, the Japanese government began to encourage the establishment of women's junior high schools. general:melon bread.name: melon_bread

rule_evidence.definition:
A sweet crispy bread, so called because its appearance resembles a melon. It traditionally does not have melon flavoring, although some manufacturers may add melon flavoring when desired. There are also many variations depending on the additional ingredients. Not limited to Japan, it is also found in Latin America as a variant of pan dulce.
Trademark food of Shana; if shown with a character who shares her voice actress, it becomes an instant voice actor connection.
Not to be confused with pineapple bun, a similar looking bread.

general:meme.name: meme
general:meme.explanation_zh: 含义取决于具体梗与上下文。

rule_evidence.definition:
A meme is an idea that spreads from person to person, especially across the internet. Memes are typically humorous images, videos, and jokes that spread across the internet, frequently being copied, parodied, adapted, and evolving over time.
Memes can take a variety of forms, from parodies of specific photos or images, to inside jokes or references, to viral internet trends or challenges, to captions or image macro (meme)s.
This tag is automatically added along with any tag with a name ending with *_(meme) When creating a new meme tag, make sure to follow this format.

general:menacing (jojo).name: menacing_(jojo)

rule_evidence.definition:
"Menacing", or ゴゴゴゴ (gogogogo), is a sound effect used in JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken, commonly used in the presence of dangerous or intimidating characters or objects. It is an example of gitaigo or "phenomime", a sound effect that represents a mood or feeling rather than an actual sound.
The tag name comes from the fact the official subtitles for the anime, provided by Crunchyroll, will often translate the text, as it appears on screen, as "Menacing".

general:mg42.name: mg42

rule_evidence.definition:
The MG42 (Maschinengewehr 42) is a German World War II-era open-bolt machine gun that fires the 7.92×57mm Mauser round. It supplanted the earlier MG34 in 1942 due to lower manufacturing cost thanks to dominant stamped metal parts. Due to its highest cyclic rate of fire that measures up to 1200 RPM, the weapon gained the nickname Hitler's Buzzsaw.
The MG42 is recognizable by its barrel shroud with squared-off profile and larger perforations. It is belt-fed and also accepts dual drum magazines.
For the post-WWII counterpart with some modernized features and synthetic furniture instead of a woode

general:miko.name: miko
general:miko.explanation_zh: 白色上衣与红色袴的示意。
general:miko.meaning_en:
A shrine maiden in a Shinto shrine.
They sweep the shrine, do ceremonial dances, perform music, flank the priest at prayers, freshen the offerings, operate the fortune telling lottery (omikuji), sell votive tablets (ema), and in most modern shrines run the knickknack and good luck charms shop. Historically, they used to be mediums and oracles, alongside the male Geki. They often carry gohei, wooden wands with paper streamers called shide.

general:mixed media.name: mixed_media

rule_evidence.definition:
Artwork in which more than one medium or material has been employed, such as a combination of traditional media and digital (computer-based) media.
Images where the use of traditional media isn't apparent to the viewer (e.g. traditional line art existed but was mostly obliterated by digital colors) count as neither traditional media nor mixed media.
Likewise, if 3D assets are used, it must be apparent that they are 3D assets. If they are traced and colored over by hand, that is not mixed media. (e.g. post #5889413)

Mohawk also counts regardless if the hair is not standing straight up from the head.

general:mullet.name: mullet
general:mullet.meaning_en:
Business in the front, party in the back.
A men's haircut that has waxed and waned in popularity since the 1970s. However, it is most associated with the 1980s, and it is considered the stereotypical male hairstyle of that period. The hair is cut short at the front and sides, but left long at the back. It has at times been associated with the rock and country music genres, lesbian subculture, and professional athletes.
A mullet with a narrow lock of hair tied or braided in the back is known as a rattail.

general:multiple views.name: multiple_views
general:multiple views.explanation_zh: 同一画面展示主体的不同视角。

rule_evidence.definition:
Two or more different pictures of the same character in an image. These can be the same character from different viewpoints, in different outfits, in different poses, or any combination.
This tag doesn't apply to zoom layers unless the zoom layer is different from the foreground image. It also doesn't apply to comics, as they generally always have multiple views. If the images form a clear sequence over time, it is probably a comic with borderless panels or a sequential image instead.
Images with multiple views should not be tagged solo, as solo is for a single view of a single character.

general:muscular female.name: muscular_female

rule_evidence.definition:
A female character with a bulky, muscular physique that must have come from extensive training, body building or otherwise.
If the character has an athletic build that's not overly bulky, use toned instead. Muscular women usually have a overall bulky physique, with thick arms and legs, not just well developed abs.
Don't tag female characters intentionally drawn to look like men (e.g. Cho Marisa with a beard, a woman drawn to look like Kenshiro, etc) as muscular females.

If the physique is muscular with a belly like many wrestlers and bodybuilders, consider adding the plump, belly and/or strongman waist tag as well.

If the character has an athletic build that's not overly bulky, use toned instead. Details like thick arms, a thick neck, a strongman waist, broad shoulders, and an overall bodybuilder physique are a good way to distinguish between toned and muscular builds.
If the physique is muscular with a belly like many wrestlers and bodybuilders, consider adding the plump, belly and/or strongman waist tag as well.

general:musical staff.name: musical_staff

rule_evidence.definition:
A set of five horizontal lines and four spaces that each represent a different musical pitch or, in the case of a percussion staff, different percussion instruments. Appropriate musical notes, depending upon the intended effect, are placed on the staff according to their corresponding pitch or function. Musical notes are placed by pitch, percussion notes are placed by instrument, and rests and other symbols are placed by convention.
When on paper, this is tagged as sheet music.

general:naval uniform.name: naval_uniform
general:naval uniform.meaning_en: A military uniform worn by members of a navy. Typically these will be either white or khaki in summer or tropical regions, and black or very dark blue in winter or cold regions. A naval dress uniform, meant for ceremonial purposes, would usually be worn for special occasions while ashore, but rarely worn on an active vessel. Conversely, a naval working uniform is the typical clothing worn while out at sea, and is usually meant more for protection than for good looks.

rule_evidence.definition:
An image relating to the first day of the new year on the Gregorian calendar.
It's a tradition for many Japanese artists to celebrate the new year by drawing girls clad in expensive kimono, eating zouni soup, carrying hamaya (a Shinto ward against evil and bad luck) and playing hanetsuki.
Many artists also pay tribute to the Chinese zodiac by incorporating whatever animal corresponds to the year. It should be noted that the Chinese new year is not on January 1 of the Gregorian calendar, but instead varies from one year to the next (falling in either late January or early February). rule_evidence.passage:
An image relating to the first day of the new year on the Gregorian calendar.
It's a tradition for many Japanese artists to celebrate the new year by drawing girls clad in expensive [[kimono]], eating [[zouni soup]], carrying [[hamaya]] (a [[Shinto]] ward against evil and bad luck) and playing [[hanetsuki]].
Many artists also pay tribute to the [[Chinese zodiac]] by incorporating whatever animal corresponds to the year. It should be noted that the Chinese new year is not on January 1 of the Gregorian calendar, but instead varies from one year to the next (falling in either late January or early February). The year of the horse, for example, begins January 31, 2014. Despite this, images utilizing the animal of an upcoming [[Chinese New Year]] tend to begin appearing around January 1, as Japan uses the same zodiac but does not use the Chinese Lunar calendar.

Also known as a "cabbie cap" or "cabbie hat".

A ninja or shinobi is a Japanese covert agent/mercenary specialized in underhanded fighting and espionage. A female ninja is called a kunoichi.
Despite many popular folktales, historical accounts of the ninja are scarce. There is little evidence that they were assassins.  Following the establishment of the Tokugawa shogunate in the 17th century, the ninja faded into obscurity.

general:noh mask.name: noh_mask

rule_evidence.definition:
A traditional Japanese theater mask.
Noh (能) is a classical Japanese form of dance drama. Noh masks are also used in Kyōgen performances (the comedic counterpart to Noh) and sometimes also in other Japanese performing arts and ceremonies.
Noh masks are traditionally made from carved cypress wood, painted or lacquered. They are frequently affixed by means of a red silk tying cord. They tend to employ heavy emphasis of shadows in order to portray different emotions (which can be changed by angling the mask).

They are recognized by their distinctive set of garments, called a habit. Christian ones can be additionally recognized by the appearance of a [[cross]] or [[crucifix]].
The term "nun" is applicable to Catholics – both Eastern and Western traditions – Orthodox Christians, Anglicans, Lutherans, Jains, [[buddhist nun|Buddhists]], and Taoists. Nuns can vary in appearance not just across each tradition, but within traditions as well; common subtypes of nuns across traditions include military nuns (or battle/combat/warrior nuns).

general:nunchaku.name: nunchaku

rule_evidence.definition:
Nunchaku, more commonly known as the "nunchucks", is a traditional East Asian weapon that consists of two sticks connected at their ends with a short chain or rope.
While often associated with Chinese and Okinawan martial arts, most long chained and small handle nunchaku were actually created in the Philippines, where they are called Tabak-Toyok and are commonly known as Chako.  The Chako is often used as a street weapon in brawls.  The smaller size of the Tabak-Toyok allows for easy concealment and everyday carry.  The weapon is best used at long-range.

general:obijime.name: obijime

rule_evidence.definition:
Obijime is a small decorative string tied around the obi, used only in women's kimono.
It's about 150 cm (4.9 ft) long and is tied around the obi and through the knot, and which doubles as decoration. It can be a woven string, or be constructed as a narrow sewn tube of fabric. There are both flat and round obijime. They often have tassels at both ends and are made from silk, satin, brocade or viscose. A cord-like or a padded tube obijime is considered more festive and ceremonial than a flat one.

general:obliques.name: obliques

rule_evidence.definition:
The muscles on the sides of the abdomen. Use this tag when the oblique muscles are well-developed and noticeable.
The external oblique muscle is one of the outermost abdominal muscles, extending from the lower half of the ribs around and down to the pelvis ending where the groin begins. Common names to describe developed obliques are "fish gills" (upper) and the Adonis or Apollo's Belt (lower).
While it is possible for females to develop this muscle, it is more visible and far more common in males due to the differences in bone structure and distribution of body fat.

general:off-shoulder coat.meaning_en:
A shoulder-less coat with a wide low-cut neckline that is designed to leave the shoulders bare, with the sleeves resting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders.
Do not use for regular coats that are partially removed, worn hanging off the arms, or worn on the shoulders like a cape. This tag is for coats that are physically designed not to cover the shoulders. If unsure, use the off shoulder tag instead.

general:off-shoulder dress.name: off-shoulder_dress
general:off-shoulder dress.meaning_en:
A shoulder-less dress with a wide low-cut neckline that is designed to leave the shoulders bare, with the sleeves resting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders.
Do not use for dresses that don't cover the arms (such as strapless or sleeveless dresses), dresses with detached sleeves, or for regular dresses that are partially removed or worn hanging off the arms. This tag is for sleeved dresses that are physically designed for the sleeves not to cover the shoulders. If unsure, use the off shoulder tag instead.

general:off-shoulder jacket.name: off-shoulder_jacket
general:off-shoulder jacket.meaning_en:
A shoulder-less jacket with a wide low-cut neckline that is designed to leave the shoulders bare, with the sleeves resting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders.
Do not use for regular jackets that are partially removed, worn hanging off the arms, or worn on the shoulders like a cape. This tag is for jackets that are physically designed not to cover the shoulders. If unsure, use the off shoulder tag instead.

general:off-shoulder leotard.name: off-shoulder_leotard
general:off-shoulder leotard.meaning_en:
A sleeved leotard with a wide low-cut neckline that is designed to leave the shoulders bare, with the sleeves resting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders. The sleeves must be attached to the leotard.
Off-shoulder leotards should not be tagged as strapless leotards.

general:off-shoulder one-piece swimsuit.name: off-shoulder_one-piece_swimsuit
general:off-shoulder one-piece swimsuit.meaning_en:
A shoulder-less one-piece swimsuit with a wide low-cut neckline that leaves both shoulders bare, with the sleeves resting on the arms instead of the shoulders.
One of the variations for the Swimsuit Lancer of Meltryllis (fate) is an example of this.
For two-piece swimsuits, see off-shoulder bikini.

general:off-shoulder shirt.name: off-shoulder_shirt
general:off-shoulder shirt.meaning_en:
A shoulder-less shirt with a wide low-cut neckline that is designed to leave the shoulders bare, with the sleeves resting on the upper arms instead of on top of the shoulders. The sleeves must be attached to the shirt.
Do not use for shirts that don't cover the arms (such as strapless shirts, sleeveless shirts, tube tops, tank tops, etc), or for regular shirts that are partially removed or worn hanging off the arms. This tag is for sleeved tops that are physically designed for the sleeves not to cover the shoulders. If unsure, use the off shoulder tag instead.

general:off-shoulder sweater.name: off-shoulder_sweater
general:off-shoulder sweater.meaning_en:
A shoulder-less sweater with a wide neckline that is designed to leave the shoulders bare, with the sleeves resting on the upper arms instead of top on the shoulders. Often ribbed and featuring a thick, sometimes mantle-like hem along the top.
Do not use for regular sweaters that are worn hanging off the arms. This tag is for sweaters that are physically designed not to cover the shoulders. If unsure, use the off shoulder tag instead.

general:offering hand.name: offering_hand

rule_evidence.definition:
A hand being offered to you, the viewer. Usually a prelude to holding hands, a handshake, being helped up off the ground, or a dance invitation. If both hands are offered, consider hugging viewer, carry me or outstretched arms instead.
For hands offering any sort of item, see {{incoming_*}}.

general:official style.name: official_style

rule_evidence.definition:
Fan art that uses the same style as official art of the series. For example, a Dragon Ball character drawn in Toriyama Akira's style, or a Touhou character drawn in ZUN's style.
Not to be confused with style parody, which is for art that mimics the style of another artist or series.
If an official artist (character designer, animator, etc.) shares fan art of their own character, but not in an official capacity, it should be tagged official artist extra instead.

general:oil lamp.name: oil_lamp

rule_evidence.definition:
An ancient form of lighting. The most basic oil lamps are simple clay cups filled with oil into which a wick is dipped. Later oil lamps are more ornate and made of materials such as bronze or silver (think of the "magic lamp" from Arabian Nights).
For more modern petroleum-burning "oil lamps", see kerosene lamp.

general:okobo.name: okobo

rule_evidence.definition:
Japanese platform sandals that were traditionally worn by geisha during their apprenticeship. The most notable type in fanart are the black-lacquered kind with red straps.
Technically, the black-lacquered finish is only worn mainly during summer, and the color of the straps used changes depending upon how far along the apprentice geisha is in her training.
Not to be confused with geta, which have two square "teeth" on the sole instead of being made as a solid block, or zouri, which are flat like flip flops.

general:old school swimsuit.name: old_school_swimsuit

rule_evidence.definition:
A school swimsuit, usually blue or black in color, with thicker shoulder straps, vertical seams over the torso, and a school swimsuit flap over the groin. Sometimes has a white name tag stitched across the chest.
If it lacks the groin flap, but is otherwise the same, it's a new school swimsuit instead; if it has thin shoulder straps distinct from the main body of the suit and lacks seams, it's a competition school swimsuit.

general:omurice.name: omurice

A Western-inspired Japanese dish that features rice cooked into an omelet, forming a pouch, and usually topped with ketchup. The ketchup is often poured to spell out words (such as the intended eater's name).
Typically, the rice is "chicken rice" fried in a pan with chicken and ketchup, but the ingredients can vary. Other variations include omusoba substituting yakisoba for the rice and omutako in Okinawa consisting of an omelet over taco rice.

general:one side up.name: one_side_up
general:one side up.meaning_en:
A hair style in which a portion of hair is tied up on one side, while the rest hangs normally. The amount of hair tied up doesn't matter, only that the untied hair falls down loosely.
The key difference between one side up and side ponytail is that in a one side up, only a small portion of hair is tied up and most of the hair hangs loosely, while in a side ponytail, most of the hair is tied up and no hair (except for sidelocks) is left hanging loose.
If the hair is not tied up but just sticking out on its own, tag as side ahoge.

general:one-piece swimsuit.name: one-piece_swimsuit
general:one-piece swimsuit.meaning_en:
A swimsuit which is worn as a single piece of clothing and provides more coverage than a bikini.
School swimsuits and competition swimsuits are two of the most common types of one-piece swimsuits. A casual one-piece swimsuit is any other swimsuit that is not one of these types.
Note that slingshot swimsuits, while technically consisting of a single piece of fabric, are not considered one-piece swimsuits.

rule_evidence.definition:
A creature from Japanese mythology. Usually translated as "demon" or "ogre".
Traditionally depicted with red or blue skin, a tiger print loincloth, and horns. Oni horns can be depicted in various ways, whether it be as long, smooth, skin-covered or otherwise the same color as the skin, located on the forehead; or cone-shaped in any number of colors, whether it be white, grey, yellow, etc. atop their head. Their weapon of choice is the spiked club, particularly the kanabou. They are violent and favor brawn over brains.
Save for the horns, modern depictions tend to mute these characteristics con

The best-known examples are probably [[Sephiroth]]'s [[Masamune (ff7)|]] in [i][[Final Fantasy VII]][/i] and the various long sword-class weapons featured in the [i][[Monster Hunter (series)|]][/i] series.
The ootachi was a rare weapon. In real life, it was used by men on foot to fight against mounted cavalry, however [[polearm]]s were much easier to produce and in most cases were more effective in that role. general:orca.name: orca

rule_evidence.definition:
The Orca (Orcinus orca) is a black and white carnivorous marine mammal. Commonly known as the killer whale and also known as orca whale. The orca is the largest species of dolphin, being part of the family Delphinidae. (Delphinidae is within the Odontoceti or toothed whales, which is within the Cetacea or whales, so orcas are whales in the sense that all dolphins are whales.)
Despite this, works portraying an Orca ought not be tagged as whale.
Usually growing around 5-8 meters long, orcas are known to be apex predators of the sea, as they have no natural predators.

The [b]Orca[/b] ([i]Orcinus orca[/i]) is a black and white carnivorous marine mammal. Commonly known as the [b]killer whale[/b] and also known as [b]orca whale[/b]. The orca is the largest species of dolphin, being part of the family Delphinidae. (Delphinidae is within the Odontoceti or toothed whales, which is within the Cetacea or whales, so orcas are whales in the sense that all dolphins are whales.)
Despite this, works portraying an Orca [b]ought not[/b] be tagged as [[whale]].
Usually growing around 5-8 meters long, orcas are known to be apex predators of the sea, as they have no natural predators.

general:pale skin.meaning_en:

Pale skin, in most cultures, is associated with nobility since they did not spend a lot of time outside and did not get the tanned skin the commoners have.
A good example of a character usually drawn with pale skin is Ayanami Rei.

It is named after Paeon, a student of Asclepius (mythology), the god of medicine and healing in Greek mythology.

rule_evidence.definition:

Also known as the 45:55 ratio or "beckoning breasts" as coined by Patrick Mallucci, who led a large research study into what defines an attractive breast.
For breasts that are the opposite of perky, see sagging breasts.

general:petticoat.name: petticoat

rule_evidence.definition:
A women's undergarment consisting of material draped from the waist and worn under a skirt or dress.
It has two purposes: to keep the skirt from riding up and to add fullness to the skirt. For the latter reason, petticoats are often heavily ruffled and comprise multiple layers. Wearing a petticoat low enough for the lace edge to be visible is a common feature of lolita fashion.

general:phrygian cap.name: phrygian_cap
general:phrygian cap.meaning_en:
A soft conical brimless hat, sometimes depicted with the top being pulled forward. Notably worn by Link and The Smurfs.
Originally associated with several peoples from Eastern Europe during antiquity, it became a symbol of liberty over the eighteenth century, notably in France where it is commonly associated with the French Revolution.
Not to be mistaken with a nightcap.

An image drawn with a pixelated art style, typically with large individual pixels and a limited color palette.

Different from oekaki, which has less emphasis on being drawn with individual pixels.

general:pixie cut.name: pixie_cut
general:pixie cut.meaning_en:
A women's hairstyle, cut very short (around cheek length or less) on the sides and back of the head, while slightly longer on top.
The amount of styling varies, but it is usually unstyled. The cut often includes swept bangs that are positioned close to the eyes, creating a flattering and accentuated facial profile. They are typically low-maintenance, require minimal styling, and are a practical option for those who lead active lifestyles.
The hairstyle is often commonly associated with tomboy characters.

Modern pizza originated from the Neapolitan pizza from Naples, Italy. It is one of the most popular fast food in the world.
There are also dessert pizzas that use chocolate, cream, candy and other sweet ingredients to create a treat resembling pizza.

general:plum blossoms.name: plum_blossoms

rule_evidence.definition:
The blossoms of plum trees, especially of the genus Prunus mume. The petals are white, pink or red, and bloom in early spring.
Distinguished from cherry blossoms in that cherry petals have slits at the ends of the petals. Plum petal ends on the other hand are round.
The plum blossom is the national flower of China, and is an important cultural symbol in the country. Images depicting China more often feature plum blossoms than cherry blossoms.

general:plumeria.name: plumeria

rule_evidence.definition:
A genus of flowering plants in the family Apocynaceae. Most species are deciduous shrubs or small trees that grow in tropical regions. One of the most commonly depicted species is Plumeria rubra, also known as frangipani.
Plumeria flowers are five-petaled with finely defined, overlapping petals. The petal tips are usually rounded. Flowers can be of various colors, but most are multicolored.
In anime art, it is frequently used in beach scenes as a hair ornament or part of a flower necklace.

general:pointless censoring.name: pointless_censoring

rule_evidence.definition:
Censorship that fails to properly conceal the object in question. Examples include bar censors that barely obscure the object, or mosaic censoring that is barely visible.
A complete lack of censorship is generally frowned on by Japanese publishers due to the self-censorship policy as a result of the Article 175 of the Japanese law forbidding all kind of pornography within Japan, so artists will use techniques seen here in order to avoid confrontation or prosecution.
See fake censor when something that doesn't need to be censored is censored as a joke, such as bad food.

general:poke ball.name: poke_ball

rule_evidence.definition:
A spherical capsule used to capture and store Pokémon. The most common and recognized Poké Ball is the basic Poké ball, which has two colored halves: red on top and white on bottom. It is one of the central symbols of the franchise. Known as a Monster Ball in Japan.
Normally, captured Pokémon are shrunken down and stored inside the ball, though some refuse to go inside the Poké Balls. Ash's Pikachu is a notable example.
Some Pokémon are noticeably similar to Poké Balls: Voltorb, Electrode (pokemon), Foongus, Amoonguss, Galarian Stunfisk, and Brute Bonnet.

general:polaroid photo.name: polaroid_photo

rule_evidence.definition:

Before the introduction of postage stamps, recipients were unable or unwilling to pay for delivered items, and senders had no incentive to restrict the number, size, or weight of items sent. The postage stamp resolved this issue in a simple and elegant manner, with the additional benefit of room for an element of beauty to be introduce

rule_evidence.passage:
One of two symbols composed of a Zero (Circle) and One (vertical line) overlaid on top of each other.
Under the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 60417 standard, Graphical symbols for use on equipment, 0 is the symbol for "off" and 1 is the symbol for "on." Combining these two symbols you get either the symbol for "on/off" (a circle with a vertical line inside of it) or "stand-by" (an incomplete circle with an opening at the top and a vertical line sticking out of the opening).  For electronics it is very common to see the "Standby" symbol used nowadays, as the electronic device does not completely turn off but instead goes into a low power state.
The symbol in [[Purple Heart (neptunia)|]]'s eyes in images like post #1151905 is an example of the "stand-by" symbol.

Combining these two symbols you get either the symbol for "on/off" (a circle with a vertical line inside of it) or "stand-by" (an incomplete circle with an opening at the top and a vertical line sticking out of the opening). general:qixiong ruqun.name: qixiong_ruqun

rule_evidence.definition:
Qixiong ruqun is a style of traditional Chinese clothing hanfu, consisting of a long-sleeved blouse or jacket and a high-waisted skirt that reaches just below the armpits, covering the chest. It was most popular during the Tang Dynasty (618–907 CE) and is one of the best-known ruqun variations.
This style was commonly worn during periods of Han Chinese rule and is categorized as hanfu. It often featured flowing fabrics, intricate patterns, and vibrant colors, reflecting the aesthetic preferences of the Tang era.
Not to be confused with other forms of ruqun.

general:ramen.name: ramen
general:ramen.meaning_en:
A Japanese wheat-flour noodle soup dish popular in East Asian cuisine, derived from Chinese 'lamian' noodles.
It is made by serving ramen noodles in beef or fish broth that is flavored with soy sauce or miso (food), and topped with a variety of items such as char siu, seaweed, heimuer, narutomaki, softboiled egg, chopped spring onion and kamaboko. There are different flavor distinctions for ramen, such as shio (salty), tonkotsu (pork bone), shoyuu (soy), hiyashi (chilled) and miso.

general:randoseru.name: randoseru

rule_evidence.definition:
A style of backpack worn by elementary schoolchildren in Japan.
Its name is derived from the Dutch "ransel". It's a firm leather pack with a single large flap that curves over the top. The traditional colors are red for girls and black for boys. Additional colors have been available since the 1960's, but culturally only took off after the 2000's. Black is still the preferred color for boys, but the preferred color for girls has shifted to lavender purple, peach pink, and light blue over red.
These bags are expensive, averaging around ¥60,000, but are intended to last through the entirety of el

general:ranguage.name: ranguage

Written text with broken spelling or grammar.
What you get when a non-native speaker tries to use a language they're not fluent in, and makes mistakes in the process. That country is usually Japan in Danbooru's case, but other international screwups are possible and encountered. These mistakes can include both misspellings (such as the very common error of mixing up "L" and "R") and grammatical errors. Sometimes the speaker also is too young to speak their native language properly.

general:rash guard.name: rash_guard

rule_evidence.definition:
A athletic shirt worn when surfing, snorkeling, jet skiing, or doing other watersports.
Most rash guards have long sleeves, and while some women's tops show midriff, most are regular shirt length. They are sometimes worn under a wetsuit or diving suit for added comfort.
Not to be confused with a wetsuit or one-piece swimsuit. If there is no line between the top from bottom pieces, assume the garment is a wetsuit instead.

general:recorder.name: recorder

rule_evidence.definition:
A family of woodwind instruments.  The most common type are soprano recorders, with low cost plastic versions frequently issued to school children since the 20th century.
It is played perpendicular to a person's lips through a mouthpiece called a fipple or block. It has a slightly tapering body with eight finger holes and can come in a variety of colors. The name comes from one of the meanings of the word record, which is "to practice a piece of music."
A recorder needs to have a whistle (shaped) mouthpiece.

A reference sheet usually consists of multiple views of the same subject from different angles, with notes pointing out the details of the design, and sometimes with details such as clothing or accessories drawn separately for characters. The image often has the character with certain clothes on and off.
For characters depicted in the same pose but in different clothing, use variations.
This tag is for reference sheets of any subject. Use the weapon focus and vehicle focus tags alongside this one when appropriate.

general:reichsadler.name: reichsadler

The Reichsadler ("Imperial Eagle") is a German heraldic emblem used since the Holy Roman Empire as a symbol of the German State, adopted by the German Empire as the national emblem. Its use as the National Emblem continued under the Weimar Republic. The Weimar version was re-adopted by the West Germany and modern-day Federal German Republic as the Bundesadler.

general:retrofuturism.name: retrofuturism

rule_evidence.definition:
An art movement based around the future as depicted by the people of the past. Retrofuturistic art tends to feature architectural and fashion design styles of the '60s and '70s, recently-obsolete technology, a focus on space exploration, rounded and freeform shapes, bright colors, and other elements common within depictions of the future throughout history.
On average, retrofuturistic art tends to have a more optimistic outlook towards the future, as opposed to the dystopian cyberpunk depictions common in modern sci-fi.

general:rice hat.name: rice_hat

rule_evidence.definition:
A cone-shaped hat made of straw or matting traditionally worn by rice harvesters in several Asian countries. It is kept in place by a chinstrap or an internal headband. It can be dipped in water and worn as an impromptu evaporative cooling device.
Very similar to ajirogasa, a hat made of wicker or bamboo that is worn by priests, not farmers.
A variant made of metal, wood or hardened leather worn by soldiers and samurais is called jingasa.

rule_evidence.definition:

Rina is not good at conveying emotions on her face. Because of this, she makes use of the "Rina-chan Board", a sketchbook that she draws her emotions on.

general:rocket launcher.name: rocket_launcher

rule_evidence.definition:

For tagging purpose and despite the technical distinctions, recoilless rifle is aliased into rocket launcher due to identical external appearance of the specific models and the same purpose of both weapon classes.
See missile pod for vehicle mounted rocket and missile systems.

general:salute.name: salute
general:salute.explanation_zh: 敬礼；一只手抬到额侧，另一只手臂自然放下。
general:salute.meaning_en:
A gesture of greeting and respect, typically a hand raised in the air.
Salutes vary across countries and even within different branches of the military in the same country. American salutes consist of the forearm at a 45° angle to the forehead, with the blade hand with palm towards face. British salutes are similar, but with the palm facing outward. The straight-arm salute (also called the Roman or Nazi salute) has the arm extended straight out and upwards.
A salute should not be confused with simple waving or making the V sign.

general:sandwich.name: sandwich
general:sandwich.meaning_en:
A food item consisting of two pieces of bread with one or more fillings between them. Different from a burger because sandwiches don't have a beef patty between them, instead using cold cut meats or warmed slices of meat.
While the sandwich has existed for a long time, the food got it's current name from John Montagu, the 4th Earl of Sandwich (13 November 1718 – 30 April 1792), who depending on sources, had his chefs make a roast beef between two slices of bread for him to eat while the Earl was busy playing cards with his friends or doing paperwork at his job in the British Royal Navy.

The most extreme form is called shihakugan, meaning "four-white eyes".

general:sarong.name: sarong
general:sarong.meaning_en:
A large sheet of fabric worn around the waist as a skirt, usually over a bikini. It's usually tied into a knot at one side of the hip.
The Japanese word for sarong is パレオ (pareo). Strictly speaking, a pareo and a sarong are different garments: the former originated in Tahiti, the latter in Indonesia and Malaysia. In their traditional, native forms they might be distinguished. However they are usually equivalent in common usage.

general:sash.name: sash
general:sash.meaning_en:
A large and usually colorful ribbon or band of material worn around the body, usually either draped diagonally from one shoulder to the opposite hip, or wrapped horizontally around the waist.
The waist sash may be worn as daily attire, but the shoulder sash is typically worn on ceremonial occasions only. Ceremonial sashes may also be seen in a V-shaped format, draping from both shoulders to the stomach like a large necklace.
An obi is considered a type of sash that wraps around the waist.

It may also have a shoulder strap, but this is rarely depicted. Additionally, this style of bag can also have a strap fastened on the back and can be worn like a [[backpack]].
The modern style looks like a small blue sports bag or [[duffel bag]], with a zipper on the top and a strap on each side. The straps are typically big enough to be worn over the shoulder like a [[shoulder bag]], or sometimes on the back like a [[backpack]].

A uniform commonly worn by students. Designs vary across countries, but in Japan, the two most common designs are the serafuku for girls and the gakuran for boys.

general:scouter.name: scouter

Not to be confused with the monocle, another single-lens eyepiece used expressly for correcting vision like glasses.

Other names associated with octopus girls are Cecaelia and Dagon.

general:scythe.name: scythe
general:scythe.meaning_en:
A traditional long handled agricultural tool used to harvest whole plants, such as hemp or wheat. Commonly depicted as a weapon of choice used by the Grim Reaper as a tool to reap souls, or by other mythological beings.
Although often seen in fantasy and anime as a weapon, it is only tangentially connected to the "war scythe", which is a polearm having more in common with a glaive (polearm), fauchard or naginata than with the original tool.

general:seal (animal).name: seal_(animal)

rule_evidence.definition:
A large, fish-eating mammal that has a round body, sleek fur, and lives near the sea, usually in cold climates.
Not to be confused with the sea lion. A seal is big and round with high body fat, holes for ears (excepting the fur seal and often squishes its head inward inside of its own body fat. A sea lion has a thinner body, visible ear flaps, more defined and protruding head shape, can stand "upright" on its flippers which it uses to walk, and makes loud barking sounds.

general:shell casing.name: shell_casing

rule_evidence.definition:
An empty, spent ammunition casing or shotgun shell.
This applies only to the empty casing left over after firing, not to unfired, live ammunition or intact cartridges. The shell casing is the hollow metal or plastic tube that originally held the bullet, gunpowder, and primer before the firearm was discharged.
On Danbooru, these empty casings are most often seen being ejected one at a time from a semiautomatic firearm or shotgun, in a rapid sequence from a machine gun, or manually dumped from a revolver cylinder (all at once, typically six at a time).

general:shikishi.name: shikishi

rule_evidence.definition:
Shikishi is a particular format of paperboard for art, calligraphy, poetry and autographs. Recognizable by its squarish dimensions, it also has characteristic edges which are often evident in posts that are photo (medium)s of traditional media pieces.
As it is popularly used by artists drawing sketches to give away at conventions, the term is sometimes used to describe such drawings as well. These are often autographed, dated and/or inscribed with the name of the convention (and artist's booth number). Marker (medium) is a common medium for these.
Sanseido Daijirin gives two dimensions for shi

general:shinai.name: shinai

rule_evidence.definition:
A kendo practice sword made of four bamboo slats, held together with white leather fittings at the handle, the tip, and around 3/4ths up the length of the "blade".
It is the standard wooden training weapon for sparring and formal competitions in kendo, as its construction gives it more flex which makes it unlikely to injure competitors when the associated armor is being worn (see bougu).
Do not confuse with a bokken, which is a practice sword made out of solid wood. A bokken more closely resembles a real katana in shape and does not have leather fittings. A shinai is straight rather than curve

general:shotgun.name: shotgun
general:shotgun.meaning_en:
A smoothbore gun that fires shells containing pellets, rifled slugs, or other munitions.
Shotguns have short effective range but high close-range destructive power due to the spread of the pellets. Shotguns generally have smoothbore barrels for firing multiple projectiles at once or in quick succession.

general:shotgun shell.name: shotgun_shell

rule_evidence.definition:
Ammunition for a shotgun, also known as a shotshell. Tubular in shape and with a brass base, the shell is often made of plastic of various colors, most often red. It can contain various types of projectiles, such as pellets that spread out against close range targets, or solid slug.
They often appear tucked into a bandolier on the waist, or on the side of the shotgun.
Use shell casing instead if the shell has been fired and is now empty. Also use casing ejection if the shell is being ejected from the gun's ejection port.

general:shoujo kitou-chuu.name: shoujo_kitou-chuu

rule_evidence.definition:
The standard loading message on Touhou games (as rendered in English) is "Girls do their best now and are preparing. Please watch warmly until it is ready."  It has given rise to a popular snowclone in Touhou images of "Girls are verbing" or "Girl is verbing" (and sometimes other substitutions, by the nature of snowclones.)  Use this tag when the image contains this meme in its text, or text derived from this meme.
A more literal translation of the phrase into English would be "girls are praying".

general:shuriken.name: shuriken

rule_evidence.definition:
A shuriken, commonly known as "throwing stars", is a traditional Japanese concealed weapon that was generally for throwing, and sometimes stabbing or slashing.
They are sharpened hand-held blades made from a variety of everyday items such as needles, nails, and knives, as well as coins, washers, and other flat plates of metal. Though it is commonly depicted in popular culture as a multiple bladed (usually three or four) throwing weapon with a hole in the middle as a holding point.
This weapon is commonly used by ninjas.

This weapon is commonly used by [[ninja]]s.

general:sideways mouth.name: sideways_mouth

rule_evidence.definition:
A quirk of manga/anime art where a character's face is viewed from the side, yet their mouth is drawn on the side of their face, rather than on the front.
Often the lips are still drawn on the front of the face, making it appear as if the character has two mouths.
One reason this may be done is to show more of the character's facial expression when it wouldn't otherwise be visible. Another reason is that, in animation, it's faster and easier to draw the mouth on the side than to animate the entire mouth opening normally, which would include having to adjust the jawline and lips.

A hasty or undetailed drawing often made as a preliminary study. Traits include rough lines, monochrome or basic coloring, and left over structural shapes.
Abbreviated on Pixiv as "rkgk", which comes from the Japanese word for sketch (らくがき, 落書き, rakugaki). Not all pictures tagged as "sketch" by the artist should be tagged as sketch on Danbooru. The picture must look like a sketch for it to apply. Translated tags have been removed from this wiki, because artists tend to use this tag in a very misleading way. general:skin tight.name: skin_tight

rule_evidence.definition:
Clothing that is extremely form-fitting.
Skin tight clothing usually leaves no space between the skin and the clothing. Common examples include bodysuits, leotards, swimsuits, sportswear, and other clothing made of spandex, latex, or other tight stretchable materials. Often, the clothing is so tight that cameltoe, covered nipples, covered abs, or covered navels are visible.
See tight clothes for regular clothing that is tight, but not skin tight. See impossible clothes for clothing that is unrealistically skin tight, especially around the chest.

Historically, when these types of buildings began to be built in the 1880s, the term first referred to buildings of 10 to 20 stories. Skyscrapers include offices, hotels, residential space, and retail space.

general:sledgehammer.name: sledgehammer

rule_evidence.definition:
A large hammer typically intended to be used with both hands that has a long shaft and a flat hammerhead, usually made of metal. They're frequently used for demolition, and are sometimes equipment used by police for raids for forced entry onto properties. They're also used in other applications, such as driving down railroad spikes or in shaping heavy slaps of iron.
Sledgehammers can distribute their force over a wider area, unlike most other hammers that concentrate their force to a relatively small area. This makes them similar to mallets.

Most depictions of sleeve garters will typically be tied to outfits worn in the latter 19th century or early 20th century, such as outfits of barbershop quartets or US Prohibition Era bartenders.
If worn over the bare arm, then use arm garter instead.

On Pixiv, the tag "アメリカンスリーブ":http://dic.pixiv.net/a/%E3%82%A2%E3%83%A1%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AB%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B9%E3%83%AA%E3%83%BC%E3%83%96 (American Sleeve) is used to denote a kind of sleeveless clothing where the armholes are cut near the base of the neck to the lower armpit, leaving a large portion of the shoulders bare. This is also typically a [[sleeveless turtleneck]].
This tag may be used for tops with [[detached sleeves]], but not for [[strapless]], [[off-shoulder shirt|off-shoulder]], or [[spaghetti strap]] tops. See the differences below.

general:sleeveless.meaning_en:
A shirt, dress, or other top with a neck but without sleeves, often revealing bare arms.
On Pixiv, the tag アメリカンスリーブ (American Sleeve) is used to denote a kind of sleeveless clothing where the armholes are cut near the base of the neck to the lower armpit, leaving a large portion of the shoulders bare. This is also typically a sleeveless turtleneck.
This tag may be used for tops with detached sleeves, but not for strapless, off-shoulder, or spaghetti strap tops. See the differences below.

general:sleeveless bodysuit.name: sleeveless_bodysuit
general:sleeveless bodysuit.label_zh: 无袖包覆身体的连体衣
general:sleeveless bodysuit.explanation_zh: 无袖包覆身体的连体衣。

general:sleeveless dress.name: sleeveless_dress
general:sleeveless dress.meaning_en:
A dress that is sleeveless, having a neck but no attached sleeves. It may have detached sleeves, since the dress itself is still sleeveless.
Do not confuse this tag as a "catch-all" tag for dresses with bare shoulders. If it has sleeves that sit on the arms instead of on the shoulders, it is an off-shoulder dress instead. If it has no straps or sleeves, it is a strapless dress instead.

general:sleeveless jacket.name: sleeveless_jacket
general:sleeveless jacket.meaning_en: A jacket without sleeves. The easiest way to differentiate a sleeveless jacket from a vest is that the jacket comes with a collar and are often more protective against weather, vests also seldom come with a hood compared to sleeveless jackets. Amano Hina is commonly depicted wearing a hooded, sleeveless jacket.

general:sleeveless kimono.name: sleeveless_kimono
general:sleeveless kimono.meaning_en: A kimono that does not have attached sleeves.

general:sleeveless shirt.name: sleeveless_shirt
general:sleeveless shirt.meaning_en:
A shirt that has a neck, but that doesn't have any straps or sleeves.
Shirts that have straps, such as camisoles, tank tops, and spaghetti strap tops, aren't considered sleeveless because they don't have a neck. Likewise, strapless tops such as tube tops and off-shoulder shirts aren't considered sleeveless either, because they also don't have a neck. A sleeveless shirt is like a regular shirt with a neck and shoulders, but with the sleeves removed.
A sleeveless shirt may have detached sleeves or elbow gloves, since those are separate from the shirt.

rule_evidence.definition: A shrug (clothing) that is sleeveless.
rule_evidence.passage: A [[shrug (clothing)|]] that is [[sleeveless]].

general:sleeveless sweater.name: sleeveless_sweater
general:sleeveless sweater.meaning_en:
A sweater that is sleeveless. It may have detached sleeves.
Not to be confused with a sweater vest. A sleeveless sweater usually has a turtleneck and is worn by itself, while a sweater vest usually has a v-neck and is worn over a long sleeved shirt.

general:sleeveless turtleneck.name: sleeveless_turtleneck
general:sleeveless turtleneck.meaning_en: A sleeveless garment with a turtleneck. Often a turtleneck sweater.

general:sleeveless turtleneck leotard.name: sleeveless_turtleneck_leotard
general:sleeveless turtleneck leotard.meaning_en: A sleeveless leotard with a high collar

rule_evidence.definition:

Does not include long sleeves that have been rolled up or pushed up to this length.

Usually a result of extremely baggy or oversized clothes.

general:sleeves rolled up.name: sleeves_rolled_up

rule_evidence.definition:
When a character wears their clothes with both or one of its sleeves rolled up. This can be either to cool themselves off, to prevent the sleeves from getting dirty or wet, because of clothing regulations, or because of their taste in fashion.
Includes sleeves visibly only folded up once. Not to be confused with sleeves pushed up, in which case the sleeves are only pushed up the arm, instead of being folded up.

general:sliding doors.name: sliding_doors

rule_evidence.definition:
Doors that are designed to slide open and closed, rather than being controlled by a doorknob.
Japanese homes commonly have paper sliding panels called shouji and fusuma. Shouji have a wooden lattice frame while fusuma are flat.
In homes, sliding doors are pulled open with a handle. In businesses such as convenience stores or grocery stores, they may open automatically.

general:slingshot swimsuit.name: slingshot_swimsuit

rule_evidence.definition:
A slingshot swimsuit, also known as a sling bikini or mankini for males, is a V-shaped swimsuit that stretches from the crotch, separates to cover the nipples, up over the shoulders and around the neck. It's much like a thong that stretches to go over the shoulders, providing minimal coverage to the wearer.
Slingshot swimsuits can have a V-shaped top, or have an X-shaped criss-cross halter top that crosses beneath the neck, similar to a pretzel bikini.
A common gag is that the straps fail to completely cover the nipples.

general:slippers.explanation_zh: 拖鞋；露趾、单片鞋面与开放的后跟。

A type of soft closed-toe, flat heeled shoe meant to be worn indoors.
Not to be confused with sandals. Slippers have a soft sole and usually cover the toes, while sandals have rigid soles and usually don't cover the toes.

general:slit pupils.name: slit_pupils
general:slit pupils.meaning_en:
Pupils that are "non-circular" that appear to be stretched vertically or horizontally.
These style of eyes are commonly seen with animals like small felines, foxes, goats, lizards, snakes, and cephalopods. It is a common feature of fantasy creatures such as dragons, vampires, demons and other monster characters, as well.
Tsurime eyes sometimes have large irises with a pupil appearing slit, but this isn't sufficient to be actual "slit pupils". This is also distinct from ].

general:smelling.name: smelling

rule_evidence.definition: The act of inhaling air with the nose to determine what a particular scent is. Smells can be perceived when odor molecules bind to hair-like neurons in the nose called cilia. Pleasant smells can invoke happiness and nostalgia, while bad odors can cause revulsion and force the person to cover their nose. It is of the five senses, also called olfaction.

general:smug.explanation_zh: 常见为半眯眼和偏向一侧的笑容。
general:smug.meaning_en:
Exhibiting great satisfaction with oneself or with one's situation. This may be to the point of being overly confident or cocky, much to the annoyance of others (until, that is, one's cockiness backfires and results in failure).
The exhibitor may have a light smile or smirk on their face, half-closed or fully closed eyes, and may have their arms crossed in front of them.

general:sneezing.name: sneezing

rule_evidence.definition:
A single, involuntary reflex where the lungs fully inhale and sharply exhale through the mouth and nose to eject parasites and dust from the breathing system. Can be caused by disease and irritating dust. Differs from a cough, which is only through the mouth and is used to clear the airway, a sneeze is more like scratching an itch inside the nose.
Japanese folklore says that you sneeze when someone is talking about you behind your back.

general:sniper rifle.name: sniper_rifle

rule_evidence.definition:
A high-precision rifle designed to accurately engage targets at long range, equipped with a telescopic sight most of the time. Most modern sniper rifles feature a buttstock with adjustable length and cheekpiece position, as well as a (detachable) bipod for stability. Some of them fire specialized rounds such as the .338 Lapua Magnum, while many models share the same ammunition with the more common service rifles, such as 7.62×51mm NATO.
This tag also apply to World War II-era or earlier conventional full-length rifles with a long range scope, such as the Mosin-Nagant.

general:snout.name: snout

rule_evidence.definition:
The protruding portion of an animal's face, consisting of its nose, mouth, and jaw. In many animals, the equivalent structure is called a muzzle, rostrum, or proboscis.
Snouts are found on many mammals in a variety of shapes. Some animals, including ursines and great cats, have box-like snouts, while others, like shrews, have pointed snouts. Pig snouts are flat and cylindrical.
Furry characters often show their snouts on a profile view, similarly to how human anime characters only show the contour of their noses on a profile view.

When on paper, this is tagged as sheet music.

general:steamed bun.name: steamed_bun

rule_evidence.definition:
A type of steamed, filled bun or bread-like dumpling originating in China, with regional varieties in many world cuisines. There are many variations in fillings (meat or vegetarian) and preparation (usually steamed).
In China, it is known as baozi. It is derived from the traditional Chinese mantou, a steamed bun without fillings (although regionally mantou may refer to baozi as well).
In Japan, it is known as manjuu, the Japanese rendering of mantou. A meat-filled manjuu is a nikuman; those referred to as manjuu typically have a sweet filling.

general:stiletto (weapon).name: stiletto_(weapon)

rule_evidence.definition:
A stiletto is a kind of dagger, optimized to function as a stabbing weapon exclusively. Generally it has little to no cutting edges, being essentially a long, thin spike with a needle-like point mounted to a handle.
The stiletto originated in late 15th century Italy.  As a result of its abilities to penetrate thick clothing and even mail, and to inflict lethal wounds with comparatively less external bleeding, as well as being easy to conceal, it became the favored weapon of the medieval assassin.
Notably used by Yor Briar.

general:street.name: street
general:street.meaning_en:
A paved road in a city environment, usually designed for both vehicle and pedestrian traffic.
A street is a type of road. The difference between a road and a street is that road is for all types of roads, including highways and dirt roads outside of cities, while a street generally refers to a paved road in a city. A street is usually designed to accommodate both vehicle and pedestrian traffic, with intersections, traffic lights, sidewalks, and crosswalks. A highway is usually designed only for high-speed or long distance vehicle traffic and doesn't have these features.

general:sukajan.name: sukajan

rule_evidence.definition:
A jacket in the style of a bomber jacket or letterman jacket with embroidery on the back and chest, often of fancy eastern-themed designs such as eastern dragons, tigers, cherry blossoms, etc.
The sukajan has its origins in post-World War II, where occupying American soldiers in Japan would commemorate their time overseas by ordering custom-made jackets with these oriental designs. For this reason, these jackets are also known as souvenir jackets.
Often seen worn by delinquents, the yakuza, or band (music) members.

It evolved into the more realistic Real Robot (リアルロボット, Riaru Robotto) anime genre started by Tomino Yoshiyuki's Mobile

general:surgical mask.name: surgical_mask

rule_evidence.definition:
A mouth mask of the type worn by doctors and nurses to prevent the spread of bacteria from the wearer's mouth and nose.  It is composed of a rectangular piece of cloth with several horizontal folds to allow it to stretch over the mouth and nose.
This term refers to two similar types of medical masks, a procedure mask and surgical mask. Procedure masks may not be sterile and fasten by looping around the ears; used when carrying out general medical procedures like a check-up. Surgical masks are sterile and are fastened by bands that loop around the head; used when carrying out surgeries.
In Japa

Sweet Lolita or "Amaloli" ( アマーロリ ) is a substyle of Lolita fashion heavily influenced by Rococo styles as well as Victorian and Edwardian children's clothing. Focusing on the child and fantasy aspects of Lolita, the Sweet Lolita style adopts the basic Lolita format and uses lighter colors.
It has all the traditional Lolita elements but with a wider choice of colors, like light pinks, baby blues, whites, and even sometimes colors like lavender, canary yellow and mint green. This is also where you'll find the most fluff and frills.

general:sweet potato.name: sweet_potato

rule_evidence.definition:
Also called a camote, it is a type of tuber vegetable that isn't as starchy as the potato, but instead has a sweeter taste. Tends to be mislabeled as a yam, but they are from an entirely different botanical species. This is also known as a food that makes you gassy. Hence why you see many artists draw fart illustrations as part of the gag.
In Mexico, Bolivia, Peru, Chile, Central America, and the Philippines, the sweet potato is known as camote
Popularly associated with Aki Minoriko because she wears a sweet potato-scented perfume, and has a spellcard named after them in Mountain of Faith.

general:sword.name: sword
general:sword.meaning_en:
A bladed weapon designed for cutting or thrusting. They are typically composed of a hilt and a blade with one or two edges that can be straight or curved; most, but not all, swords have a pointed tip. The hilt, in turn, consists of a guard, a grip, and in most designs a pommel. The guard can be a crossguard like in a typical knight's sword, a disc like the tsuba (guard) of a katana, or some more complex design.
It is a weapon strongly associated with elite warriors such as knights and samurai.

general:sword tassel.name: sword_tassel

rule_evidence.definition:
A decorative tassel attached to the hilt of a sword.
They are used to help secure the sword to the wielder's wrist while in use, preventing the sword from being dropped or knocked out of the hand during combat. Sword knots are often made of braided leather or silk and can be intricately designed with tassels, fringe, or other embellishments.
In addition to their practical function, sword knots also serve a ceremonial or decorative purpose, adding a touch of elegance to the overall appearance of the sword.

This tag is used to describe a hypodermic needle, which is a hollow needle commonly used to inject substances into the body or used to take liquid samples from the body. However, the needle portion itself need not be present for the tag to qualify.
Syringes are called needles in some areas of the world, but on Danbooru, needles refer to the thin stick of pointed metal used for sewing or as weapons.
Use of syringes may cause track marks.

Should not be confused with polo shirts, a pull-over shirt that features a collar, or short sleeve dress shirts.

Not to be confused with a surcoat, which is also worn over armor, but which is longer and has closed sides.

general:tabi.name: tabi
general:tabi.meaning_en:
Traditional Japanese split-toe socks with a division between the big toe and the other toes in order to be worn with sandals.
Historically, tabi were commonly made of inelastic materials such as leather and cotton and had fasteners at the back due to their origin as indoor footwear. Modern tabi use stretchable fabrics.
For socks with a division between all toes, use toe socks instead. For tabi that are worn as shoes, use jika-tabi instead.

general:table.meaning_en: A piece of furniture with a flat horizontal upper surface.

general:tablet pc.name: tablet_pc
general:tablet pc.meaning_en:
A tablet computer, commonly just called a tablet, is a portable computer housed within the casing of a handheld touchscreen display.  They appear like a larger version of the modern smartphone.
Unlike laptops, tablet computers lack a built-in keyboard.  Should not be confused with a 2-in-1 laptop, which is a laptop that features a touchscreen with the ability to flip or rotate so the display can conceal the laptop keyboard.
A popular example of a tablet computer is the iPad.

rule_evidence.definition:

Doves don't have a use for talons as they do not hunt to feed themselves; doves have claws, but no talons.
Harpies are commonly depicted with them.

general:tanghulu.name: tanghulu

rule_evidence.definition:
A traditional Chinese snack of candied fruit. Tanghulu are often mistaken for regular candied fruits; however, they are coated in a hardened sugar syrup. This sweet and sour treat has been made since the Song Dynasty and remains popular throughout northern China.
The most common fruit used for tanghulu is shanzha (fruit), but you can also find other variants with strawberry, mandarin orange, kiwi (fruit), etc.
Not to be confused with candy apple or dango.

general:tangzhuang.name: tangzhuang

rule_evidence.definition:
A tangzhuang (Simplified Chinese: 唐装) is a kind of pseudo-traditional Chinese jacket, typically with a mandarin collar.
It originated at the end of the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911) as an evolution of the Manchurian magua, which had been adopted by the Han Chinese during the Qing Dynasty. At that time, only noblemen, aristocracy and government officials wore it, however, in modern times it was eventually adopted by common people. This kind of clothing is often seen as a national costume for men, although women wear it as well.
Saotome Ranma from Ranma 1/2 is usually seen wearing this type of jacket

general:tanuki.name: tanuki

rule_evidence.definition:
The Japanese name for the Japanese raccoon dog. In Japanese mythology, a tanuki is a playful shape-shifting traditional youkai.
Not to be confused for the raccoon, which looks similar to the tanuki but is not the same animal. A key difference is their fur color: tanuki tend to have brown fur while raccoons have grey fur.
The words "tanuki" (狸), "mujina" (貉), and "mami" (猯) were historically confused in Japan. "Mujina" and "mami" used to mean badgers in some areas, while on the other areas these terms used to mean raccoon dogs. There are some areas in which badgers were called tanuki.

general:tate eboshi.name: tate_eboshi

rule_evidence.definition:
A tate-eboshi (立烏帽子, lit. "standing eboshi cap") is a tall, cylindrical hat, traditionally black, worn by Japanese male aristocrats since the Heian period. It may sometimes have a chinstrap tied under the chin. Often worn with kariginu.
Though originally made of cloth, later versions were made of lacquered paper and other, more opaque, materials. These tend to have a very distinct, "crinkled" appearance on the outside. Today these tate-eboshi may still be seen worn by Shinto priests conducting ceremonies.
Notably worn by Mononobe no Futo and Soga no Tojiko of the Touhou series.

These masks often come painted in garish red. The long nose appeared in the fourteenth century and is said to symbolize the tengu's hatred of arrogance and prejudice.
In the Ryuuko no Ken and The King of Fighters series. Takuma Sakazaki wore this mask to don a new persona called "Mr. Karate."

general:thermos.name: thermos
general:thermos.meaning_en:
A container or vessel designed to keep liquids hot or cold for long periods of time.  This is accomplished by the container being composed of two flasks, one within the other, and joined at the neck. The gap between the two flasks is partially evacuated of air to produce a near vacuum which helps to impede the transfer of heat between the contents and the outside.
While these are known as a vacuum flask or vacuum bottle, these should not be confused with a Büchner flask used in laboratory vacuum filtration, which are also known as a vacuum flask.

general:tomato.name: tomato

rule_evidence.definition:
Considered a vegetable, particularly for culinary purposes, the tomato is botanically a fruit produced by the plant Solanum lycopersicum of the nightshade family.
The word "tomato" comes from the ancient Nahuatl word tomatl.
In the US, the US Supreme Court ruled in the 1893 case Nix v. Hedden that the tomato is legally classified as a vegetable.  This was to resolve an issue with the Tariff Act of 1883 which required a tax be paid on imported vegetables, but not fruits.

Not to be confused with reverse trap, though there can be overlap between the two. A reverse trap is a girl with an androgynous or masculine appearance, regardless of personality. An androgynous girl may not necessarily act like a tomboy and a tomboy isn't required to look androgyno

general:torogao.name: torogao

rule_evidence.definition:
A facial expression where the character appears to be in an ecstatic, yet quiet and unresponsive state of pleasure.
The cheeks look flushed, the eyebrows are slanted downwards towards the sides, and the eyes are half-open and moist, often staring into the distance. It is common to see saliva and a half-open mouth as well. The limbs and joints may be relaxed and hanging loosely in place. May also involve heavy breathing or a contented smile.
It is often sexual in nature, but not always. It may also be seen when a character is eating their favorite food, for example.

general:tracen school uniform.name: tracen_school_uniform

The school uniform worn by the characters of Umamusume as well as their basic outfit.
The summer uniform consists of a purple sailor shirt with white accents and puffy short sleeves, a purple bowtie held with a horseshoe ornament, a pleated white skirt with a large purple back bow, and white thighhighs or over-kneehighs; as well as brown loafers with medium heels.
The winter uniform has mostly the same design, but the blouse having long sleeves with dark purple highlights. Meanwhile, the bowtie is now white, the skirt is purple instead of white, and the knee socks are purple with a white line

general:trading card.name: trading_card

rule_evidence.definition:
A card with a picture or design printed on it, designed to be collected and traded as part of a collectible card game.
Trading cards were traditionally associated with sports such as baseball (sport) and soccer. Since the release of Magic: The Gathering in the 1990s, cards designed specifically for playing games became popular enough that a new category of collectible card games emerged. These have since supplanted the traditional trading card market.
This tag applies to both trading cards present inside the image, and images of the trading cards themselves.

rule_evidence.definition:

Their duties include collecting tickets, making announcements, handling passenger needs, overseeing cargo loading/unloading, as well as coordinating with the train's engineer and overseeing the train attendants.

general:tsuba (guard).name: tsuba_(guard)

rule_evidence.definition:
The round or occasionally squarish handguard between the handle and the blade of bladed Japanese weapons, like the katana, tachi (weapon), wakizashi, tantou, naginata, etc. They contribute to the control of the arm (the right index of the fighter typically touches the tsuba), and they prevent the hand from slipping onto the blade.
The most common shapes of tsuba are round (maru gata), rounded-square (kaku gata) and four lobed (mokko) with many variations within each basic design.

general:tube dress.name: tube_dress

rule_evidence.definition:
A close-fitting casual strapless dress. Essentially a tube top extended to dress length. Tube dresses generally reach from just past the hips to knee length, and they tend to fit snugly around the legs like a pencil skirt or pencil dress.
A tube dress is strapless, which means it leaves the arms and shoulders bare and has no straps, attached sleeves, or halterneck. Do not use for dresses that have straps or sleeves, such as sleeveless dresses, pencil dresses, halter dresses, or off-shoulder dresses.

general:tube top.name: tube_top
general:tube top.meaning_en:
A form-fitting strapless top consisting of a continuous band of fabric wrapping around the torso, with the neckline stopping just above the breasts.
The length can range from covering the entire torso to covering just the breasts. If the midriff is exposed it may also be a crop top, while if only the breasts are covered it may be a bandeau. A tube top made of bandages is a sarashi.
Traditionally, the only support they provided was due to the stretchiness of the fabric. Tube tops do not have any attached sleeves, meaning that they leave the shoulders/arms and upper chest area bare.

general:tuxedo.name: tuxedo
general:tuxedo.meaning_en:
A traditional formal suit worn by men. Usually composed of a suit jacket, a pair of suit pants, a white dress shirt, a bowtie or sometimes even a necktie, cuff links, a pair of formal dress shoes, and sometimes, a waistcoat or cummerbund.
Tuxedos are usually worn to formal events, such as dinner parties, social balls or dances, and weddings.
Women can wear tuxedos either as they are or with skirts, shorts, or a leotard replacing the trousers.

general:tuxedo cat.name: tuxedo_cat

rule_evidence.definition:

Two tuxedo cats became fairly popular in memes, those being Maxwell the Cat of Spinning Cat (meme) fame, and Uni (cat) of Big Boobs fame. Only tag either if it can be explicitly confirmed that the cat in question is one or the other, otherwise stick with this tag only.

general:two side up.meaning_en:
A hairstyle in which two locks of hair are tied up on both sides of the head while the back of the hair hangs normally. The amount of hair tied up doesn't matter, only that the back of the hair falls down loosely.
Not to be confused with twintails, where all of the hair is tied up into two ponytails and nothing is left to fall freely.
Examples include Tohsaka Rin, Ultimate Madoka, Onozuka Komachi, most depictions of Kawashiro Nitori, Nena Trinity, and Souryuu Asuka Langley.

general:two tails.name: two_tails

rule_evidence.definition:

Not to be confused with twintails, which is a hairstyle, or with forked tail, which is a single tail that forks in two.

general:two-finger salute.name: two-finger_salute

rule_evidence.definition:
A gesture with the thumb, index and middle fingers extended and raised in front of the head as a form of saluting.
In Britain and other British Commonwealth countries, a "two-fingered salute" refers to an inward V gesture that is the equivalent of the middle finger. On Danbooru, a two-fingered salute is an actual salute.
Not to be confused with kuji-in, various ninja gestures that may involve extending the first two fingers, but not as a salute, nor with V or V over eye, which have the fingers spread apart and are not salutes.

general:tyrannosaurus rex.name: tyrannosaurus_rex

rule_evidence.definition:
A large theropod carnivorous dinosaur. Often referred to as "T. rex" for short, from the type specimen's scientific name Tyrannosaurus rex.
While there are at least five other species of Tyrannosaurus known to science, the type specimen T. rex is arguably the most popular species of non-avian dinosaur, stemming from the discovery of several complete fossil specimens, along with its depictions in media as an apex predator. Particularly in Jurassic Park.
Like other tyrannosaurids, Tyrannosaurus was a bipedal carnivore with a massive skull balanced by a long, heavy tail.

general:undercut.name: undercut
general:undercut.meaning_en:
A hairstyle in which the sides or back of the head are shaved or buzzed short, while the hair on top is kept long. The long portion may be swept to one side, slicked back, or left to hang in front of the face.
The undercut was first popularized during the 1910s to 1940s, before becoming fashionable again in the 2010s among both men and women.

general:undershirt.name: undershirt
general:undershirt.meaning_en:
A light typically collarless shirt or top made to be worn underneath other clothing, such as dress shirts. They're frequently plain and white.
Men may wear "wifebeater" tank top-style sleeveless undershirts, especially to accentuate a blue-collar look. For women, there may be some overlap with camisole. They may be worn in lieu of a bra by (typically younger) flat-chested girls with no need for supporting their breasts.
In terms of sportswear, the term "undershirt" usually refers to a shirt worn under most clothing (a baseball uniform, for example).

Not to be confused with the papakha, which does not have ear flaps.

rule_evidence.definition:
