Depending on the application they may be referred by various names, such as transmission pole, telephone pole, telecommunication pole, power pole, telegraph pole, and telegraph post.
Should not be confused with a transmission tower, which are large towers, frequently made of a steel lattice, used to carry high voltage electrical lines.

general:uwabaki.name: uwabaki

rule_evidence.definition:
Uwabaki(上履き, meaning 'indoor shoes') is the Japanese indoor shoes worn where outdoor shoes are prohibited, such as in schools, in gyms, or in some offices.
Often considered as school indoor shoes made of white cloth and colored rubber often with a same-colored toe and shoe sole that sometimes indicates the grade, these are usually (but not always) in a style similar to mary janes. Students change their outdoor shoes into uwabaki at the getabakos when they enter the school.
Not to be confused with loafers which is worn quite often with school uniforms, but they are not indoor shoes.

general:virtual youtuber.name: virtual_youtuber
general:virtual youtuber.explanation_zh: 屏幕中的虚拟形象与视频符号组合，不指定具体主播身份。

rule_evidence.definition:
A virtual YouTuber, or VTuber, is a content creator or personality who uses a 2D or 3D digital avatar for online videos and/or livestreaming, often assuming a character as well. Despite the name, VTubers are not limited to the YouTube platform.
The term was first popularized by Kizuna Ai, who called herself "the world's first virtual YouTuber". Many others followed suit, and the explosion in popularity of the practice lead the term to be used even outside of YouTube, with the Japanese defining VTubers based on the creator declaring themselves as such before considering additional factors.

general:wanted.name: wanted

rule_evidence.definition:
A poster distributed by police to warn the public about a criminal who is wanted for arrest. A wanted poster usually has the word "WANTED" at the top, and the fugitive's name and picture on the bottom. Sometimes a bounty or a list of their crimes is included.
In earlier times (or fictional settings), wanted posters would sometimes also read "wanted dead or alive", making the wanted criminal an outlaw in the literal sense (i.e. a person from whom the protection of the law was withdrawn and who could be killed without official repercussions by anyone).

rule_evidence.definition:

Amusingly, the phrase was originally coined as a public relations fig leaf for what was really a case of assisted exposure.

general:wariza.name: wariza

rule.phrase: sitting with the legs folded to either side

general:wariza.explanation_zh: 两膝朝前、小腿分向身体两侧的坐姿。
general:wariza.meaning_en:
Wariza (割座), also known as "w-sitting" or "reverse tailor style sitting" in English, is a sitting posture whereby the butt is on the floor and the legs are bent backwards on each side of the body. It is the traditional informal sitting style for Japanese women. If the legs are folded out to only one side, then it is called yokozuwari.
The other Japanese names are: 女の子座り (onna-no-ko-zuwari, girl's sitting), アヒル座り (ahiru-zuwari, duck sitting) or ぺたん座り (petan-zuwari, flat surface sitting). (In fact, in Japanese, wariza more commonly refers to a yoga pose.)

general:whip.name: whip

rule_evidence.definition:
An instrument with a handle and a long rope-like lash used for striking or making a cracking sound. It can be used for various purposes, including as a tool for directing animals, as a weapon, or as a fetish implement in BDSM.
The distinct loud sound of a whip "cracking" as it is swung is produced by a part of the lash breaking the sound barrier and generating a small sonic boom.
Not to be confused with a riding crop, which is a semi-rigid stick instead of a lash.

Horse that its entire coat colour is white, may also include its mane.
A white horse has mostly pink skin under its hair coat, and may have brown, blue, or hazel eyes. "True white" horses, especially those that carry one of the dominant white (W) genes, are rare. general:wolf.name: wolf

rule_evidence.definition:
Commonly known as a gray wolf, a species of canid native to the wilderness and remote areas of North America, Eurasia, and North Africa. It is the largest member of its family, with males averaging 43–45 kg (95–99 lb), and females 36–38.5 kg (79–85 lb) It is similar in general appearance and proportions to a german shepherd, or sled dog, but has a larger head, narrower chest, longer legs, straighter tail and bigger paws. Its winter fur is long and bushy, and is usually mottled gray in color, though it can range from nearly pure white, red, or brown to black.

general:yaoi.name: yaoi

rule_evidence.definition:
Any romantic or sexual interaction between males, whether mutual or one-sided. If it's mutual, consider also adding the couple tag.
A common misconception is that in Japan, "BL" denotes non-explicit content while "yaoi" denotes explicit content. In reality, "BL" encompasses both, and "yaoi" is a term used almost exclusively outside Japan. On Danbooru, "yaoi" is used for both SFW and NSFW content; use {{yaoi is:nsfw}} or {{yaoi is:sfw}} to distinguish between them.
For physical objects depicting yaoi, use yaoi (object) in combination with fujoshi, fudanshi, and/or otaku instead.

general:yugake.name: yugake

rule_evidence.definition:
A three-fingered glove used in Kyuudou (Japanese archery). A yugake is a partially fingerless glove that is worn on the right hand and generally has only three or four fingers. It covers the index finger, middle finger, and thumb, while leaving the ring and pinky fingers bare.
See archery shooting glove for the glove used in western archery, which covers the the ring, middle, and index fingers instead.

general:yuigaoka school uniform.name: yuigaoka_school_uniform

rule_evidence.definition:
The school uniform worn by the students attending the regular course at Yuigaoka Girls' High School in Love Live! Superstar!!
It consists of a white collared dress shirt with a red neck ribbon and a short grey pinafore dress. The winter uniform has an open blue jacket and the shirt is long-sleeved, while in the summer uniform there is no jacket and the shirt is short-sleeved.
There is also a separate version for the students who are part of the music program.

general:zodiac.name: zodiac

rule_evidence.definition:
The zodiac is the "band" of the night sky roughly corresponding to the solar system's ecliptic plane. Western astrologers divide it into twelve signs, named for the constellation that is nearest the position of the Sun for one-twelfth of the year.  (These periods do not quite line up with the calendar months, so that the sign of the zodiac changes around the twentieth or twenty-first of the month.)
Not to be confused with the popular brand of semi-rigid inflatable boats, the serial killer, the former-Soviet rock band, or the town of Zodiac, Missouri.

general:zoom layer.name: zoom_layer

rule_evidence.definition:
An additional layer that magnifies part of the illustration, usually a character. It's a common technique used for backgrounds in character art.
If there are small differences, such as the colors being muted, partially transparent, or in greyscale, the layer having simple transforms (such as being mirrored, scaled, or rotated), or the character having a different facial expression, then it's also a different zoom layer.
If the layer is not a copy of the base image, such as featuring a totally different perspective, pose, attire, or other characters, it's a projected inset instead.
